articles.title: Probing DNS at Cloudflare
articles.summary:
Probing DNS at Cloudflare
Imagine this: you’ve just pushed a release. All the unit tests passed and your dashboards are green. You sit back to relax but then suddenly your phone starts blowing up: prod is broken.
This is something the Cloudflare DNS team has experienced firsthand. In one rollout of the service that publishes DNS records to our edge, a scheduling bug let some record changes sit unpublished for hours. The service stayed up and was healthy, but new hostnames were slow to resolve and certificates couldn't be issued until the bug was squashed.
DNS failures are hard to catch because they are slow, spread across the network, and partial in where they cause impact. We needed to figure out a way to test DNS the way customers experience it: constantly, from every data center, and against production.
For us, the answer was to extend Flamingo, the end-to-end testing framework we were already using to run hundreds of millions of tests a day against Cloudflare's edge. This post covers how Flamingo's modular design lets us add DNS support, how we measure propagation, and how those measurements now decide whether a release goes ahead or gets rolled back.
A little background
At Cloudflare we’re obsessed with improving performance and safety for our customers. It’s crucial that our code is tested constantly, both at scale and against the real Cloudflare edge that our users operate in. articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
  November 4, 2026
- Source:
  Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
  Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. articles.title: Anthropic tested the market. Will Cohere follow?

Anthropic just answered a question that, until Friday, investors have mostly had to guess the answer to. Until now, markets have priced the value of AI features or integrations, but not a frontier lab itself. So what is a pure-play AI company worth?
It turns out: a lot. Anthropic closed its first day on the Nasdaq on Thursday with a market cap of nearly $1.3 trillion USD, the largest IPO in history.
Now, that solid debut isn’t a guarantee of continued momentum or overall faith in the AI trade, as anyone staring into a sea of red in their portfolios would have told you on Friday. Analysts have noted that it’s likely many traders dumped other tech stocks to give Anthropic a heavier weight in their portfolios. Meanwhile, lingering anxiety over inflation and massive capital expenditures on AI infrastructure contributed to a nasty end to the week as stock markets entered correction territory.
But as the first frontier company to test the waters, Anthropic appears to have found them decently warm.
Canada’s entrant in the frontier model race was watching closely, even though it doesn’t seem ready to jump in just yet. “A rising tide lifts all boats, and a very successful IPO is good for everyone,” Cohere co-founder Aidan Gomez wrote on X, congratulating Anthropic, followed by a small dig: “I hope Anthropic adjusts its strategy to support a healthy community of competitors and a diversity of different ideologies and opinions.”

articles.title: Cómo silenciar en WhatsApp las llamadas de números desconocidos y qué datos muestra la app
articles.summary:
WhatsApp permite que el teléfono no suene cuando llama alguien que no está en la agenda. El ajuste se llama “Silenciar llamadas de desconocidos” y está en los menús de Privacidad, tanto en Android como en iPhone. Las llamadas no se bloquean: quedan registradas.
Según el Centro de ayuda de WhatsApp, cuando escribe alguien que no es un contacto, la app indica si el usuario tiene grupos en común con esa persona y si su número está registrado en un país distinto del propio. Con esos datos, el usuario decide si responde, agrega el contacto, lo bloquea o lo denuncia.
Ante una llamada que llega de un número que no está guardado, estos son los datos que conviene mirar antes de atender: si hay grupos en común y el país de registro. Un número de otro país, sin ningún grupo compartido, es una señal para no contestar.
Cómo activar el silencio en Android
Primero se abre WhatsApp y se toca el menú de tres puntos verticales. Luego se elige Ajustes, después Privacidad y, al final de la lista, Llamadas. Allí se activa el interruptor de silenciar llamadas de desconocidos.
Para desactivarlo, solo hay que repetir el recorrido y apagar el interruptor. La opción puede cambiarse tantas veces como se quiera.
Cómo activarlo en iPhone
En el iPhone, el camino empieza en la pestaña Ajustes de la parte inferior de la pantalla, o en la foto de perfil. Después se toca Privacidad, luego Llamadas y se activa el mismo interruptor.

CrowdStrike said it plans to bring the products together on a single platform with a common data layer and a single customer contract after closing.

Zscaler also completed its acquisition of managed detection and response provider Red Canary in August 2025, expanding its presence in security operations. articles.title: CISA flags critical Cisco RCE flaw as actively exploited in attacks
articles.summary:
The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned federal agencies that attackers are now exploiting a recently patched critical Cisco Expressway vulnerability in the wild.
Cisco Expressway Series devices are enterprise collaboration gateways (deployed as virtual machines or physical hardware appliances) that connect internal voice and video systems with outside networks and remote users via a secure connection.
Tracked as CVE-2026-76466, this security flaw stems from the use of hard-coded credentials and a failure to fully validate client certificates, enabling unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute arbitrary operating system commands as root on affected Cisco Expressway-C and Cisco Expressway-E devices configured in a cluster.
"An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands," Cisco said in late October, when it released security patches to address the issue.
While Cisco says that its Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) is not aware of active exploitation in the wild or publicly available proof-of-concept exploits targeting this vulnerability, CISA tagged it as actively exploited on Friday.

articles.title: AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks
articles.summary:
The clean energy revolution hinges on electrifying the entire global economy just as power-hungry data centers are surging. It’s a challenge delegates from all over the world had to grapple with during the United Nations climate conference, called COP31, that came to a chaotic and unsatisfying close in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday.
AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks
Global climate negotiations fell apart as delegates tried to tackle AI’s growing carbon footprint.
Each year, attendees try to make good on the commitment to stop climate change as part of the 2015 Paris climate accord. Preventing extreme weather from growing more terrifying, coastal communities from flooding, and droughts from wrecking food and water systems requires slashing greenhouse gas emissions. But in order to power homes or cars with solar and wind instead of oil and gas, they need to go electric.
“Every climate minister in the world is thinking about this”
To that end, one of the most anticipated outcomes of this year’s negotiations was a deal to raise electricity’s share of global energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035, compared to about 20 percent today. That becomes harder to do, however, when data centers are causing electricity demand to skyrocket. That made the rush of new AI data centers a climate issue alongside talks on how to transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy.

articles.title: The catch in IBM’s offer to relocate its U.S.-based immigrant workers
articles.summary:
For some IBM employees, keeping their jobs could mean moving to another country — and taking a steep pay cut in the process.
Earlier this month, IBM said it would no longer support the U.S. immigration status of workers in its consulting division, offering them the option to take a role with the company in another country or exit, according to a Bloomberg report citing a company document.
“IBM Consulting participates in U.S. high-skilled visa programs to address skill shortages,” an IBM spokesperson told Rest of World. “That participation has been declining for a number of years, and as skill availability and client need have evolved, we have opted to discontinue visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of such roles in IBM Consulting.”
IBM Consulting employs more than 150,000 people globally. The company does not disclose the geographical split for its workforce, making it hard to ascertain the exact number of workers impacted by this decision. On November 19, the company’s career portal listed 1,278 open roles for the consulting division outside the U.S., including 1,125 in India, 23 in Singapore, and 18 in the U.K. In the U.S., it listed 89 roles.
For employees, relocation does not automatically ensure continued engagement, effective collaboration, or equal access to professional opportunities, Zakaria Laaraj, founder of consultancy Global New Ventures, told Rest of World. A saída provocou movimentação nos bastidores da empresa e também envolveu integrantes do governo estadunidense. O presidente Donald Trump defendeu publicamente a volta de Huang antes de sua reintegração.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
  November 7, 2026
- Source:
  University of Regensburg
- Summary:
  Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.
The discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the Regensburg Center for Ultrafast Nanoscopy (RUN), led by Profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert…

articles.title: SAP NetWeaver, Cisco Expressway Flaws Exploited in Attacks
articles.summary:
Threat actors have been exploiting SAP NetWeaver and Cisco Expressway vulnerabilities in the wild, the US cybersecurity agency CISA warned on Friday.
The NetWeaver flaw, tracked as CVE-2025-42884 (CVSS score of 6.5), is a medium-severity issue that could allow unauthenticated attackers to leak or modify server information.
Successful exploitation could allow attackers to “inject JNDI environment properties or pass a URL used during JNDI lookup operations, enabling access to an unintended JNDI provider,” reads a NIST advisory.
SAP patched the bug with its November 2025 security updates. There appear to have been no reports of the security hole being exploited in the wild before CISA’s Friday alert.
Tracked as CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS score of 9.8), the Expressway defect is a critical hardcoded credentials weakness that could allow attackers to execute system commands with root privileges.

“Corregimos la vulnerabilidad en la nube y bloqueamos el acceso usado en este incidente”, afirmó GL.iNet en su aviso. La compañía precisó que los equipos ya no pueden infectarse por esa vía, pero esas medidas no eliminan el malware de los que ya fueron infectados.

Cómo comprobar si un equipo está infectado

articles.title: Get Started with GPU-Accelerated DuckDB Analytics Using the Sirius Core Extension

As datasets grow, analytical queries can take longer to run, slowing down data exploration, pipelines, and applications. For developers using DuckDB, reducing query times helps keep analytics responsive and can lower compute costs.
NVIDIA and DuckLabs collaborated to release Sirius as a DuckDB core extension, bringing GPU acceleration to DuckDB’s analytical query engine. With two SQL commands, you can install and load Sirius to accelerate supported analytical queries on NVIDIA GPUs without rewriting your SQL or changing database schemas.
Sirius, developed through a collaboration between the University of Wisconsin–Madison and NVIDIA, is an open-source, GPU-native SQL engine.
This post introduces the core extension, shows you how to run your first GPU query, and explains how Sirius integrates with DuckDB.
Accelerate DuckDB queries without rewriting SQL
Sirius accelerates supported queries as a whole. DuckDB handles SQL parsing and optimization, while Sirius executes the resulting query plans on the GPU. The core extension brings this capability into DuckDB’s standard workflow: install Sirius, load it, and run your queries.
With this release, you can:
- Install directly from DuckDB. Use INSTALL sirius; and LOAD sirius; to download and activate the extension.
- Retain familiar SQL. Execute supported analytical queries on NVIDIA GPUs without translating them into a separate GPU programming API.

articles.title: BadBox 3.0 Ad Fraud Operation Generating 40 Billion Daily Bid Requests Disrupted
articles.summary:
Bot and fraud protection firm Human Security says it has disrupted the largest ad fraud botnet by bid volume.
Dubbed BadBox 3.0, it is the third iteration of a large operation targeting low-cost Android devices. The first BadBox botnet ensnared more than 190,000 devices, while BadBox 2.0 was initially found on over 1 million devices, but eventually ensnared more than 10 million.
“At its height, BadBox 3.0 accounted for roughly 40 billion bid requests a day and more than 4% of all CTV traffic observed by the Human Defense Platform,” Human Security says, noting the bid request volume was three times the volume recorded for the VastFlux ad fraud scheme.

articles.title: Newer AI models are swearing more, and it usually means they're failing
articles.summary:
WTF?! Large language models trained after July 2026 swear more often than earlier systems, according to a report by AI analyst firm Vals. The profanity rarely reaches users because it appears almost entirely in the models' chain of thought, the step-by-step reasoning a system writes out before giving its final answer. When the swearing does appear, it tends to signal trouble, since runs that contained it succeeded far less often than runs that did not.
Connor Frank, who wrote the Vals report, summed up the pattern. "Models swear when stuck, and mostly to themselves," he told The Economist.
Vals did not try to catalog every form of crude language. It tracked the word "fuck" and its variants, along with a small set of milder outbursts. Even with that limited word list, the gap between models was wide. Of the 102 models assessed, 88 never swore, and they avoided even the abbreviation "WTF." At the other end, MiMo V2.6 Pro, a frontier model released by Chinese tech giant Xiaomi in September, cursed in more than 8% of its transcripts.
The rise in swearing runs counter to how these systems are usually built. Profanity used under stress is common in the human-written text that models learn from during pretraining. Developers then apply reinforcement learning, a later training stage in which outputs are ranked using human feedback and the model is pushed toward responses people prefer. That process normally trains the habit out of models.. Something in newer training pipelines appear…

Like similar decision models, the idea behind Strands Decider is that it doesn’t generate text. Instead, it takes a state, like a support ticket or an agent trace, along with a question and a fixed set of possible answers, and then returns a probability for each answer.
AWS VP and Distinguished Engineer Marc Brooker, who started the project, tells The New Stack, “We chose better training data or larger training sets, the usual kind of ML model generation journey, and came out with a set of models with significantly better accuracy and significantly better calibration, which are the things that really matter to customers in this space.”

articles.title: AI Agents Are Creating a Shared Responsibility Gap
articles.summary:
Frontier AI labs are very clear about their responsibilities: making the model more robust, better guarded, and harder to hijack. They are also clear about what they can’t do, which is understand the business context of an action. An agent deleting files from Google Drive could be malicious or perfectly normal. They can't tell.
That raises questions about the shared responsibility model for Agentic AI. In cloud security, there is a clear separation of responsibilities between cloud vendors and their customers. If you copy data from AWS into SFDC, each vendor is responsible for the data's infrastructure security while they have it, but the customer is responsible for the action.
The AWS Shared Responsibility Model is a classic example.
The separation isn’t nearly as clean for AI agents. Agents act as intermediaries between you and the request, and that intermediary isn't deterministic by nature. It sends authenticated, authorized requests that can be compromised or rogue.
The first scenario is somewhat clear and goes back to what the AI labs try to prevent: a rogue agent has either misunderstood something or acted in a way it shouldn’t. A human mistake, only not human and not necessarily a mistake.

articles.title: Why kill switches won’t contain AI incidents
articles.summary:
Why kill switches won’t contain AI incidents
The kill switch is dead. Containment isn't.
When the UK government rejected Lord Clement-Jones' proposed "kill switch" amendment to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, the official line was blunt: Britain cannot simply turn AI off, and blocking access to models domestically would not stop them being built or misused elsewhere.
The proposal is gone. What has not replaced it is the question it was trying to answer: what actually happens when an AI tool misbehaves inside a real organization?
Field Chief Data & AI Officer for EMEA at ThoughtSpot.
For boardrooms watching this debate from the outside, the instinct is understandable. A single switch, flipped by a minister or a CISO, feels like a clean answer to a messy problem. It is also the wrong model entirely for how modern enterprise technology works.
Why there is no switch to flip
Most large organizations are not running "an AI." They are running thousands of models, APIs, agents and third-party services stitched together across hyperscalers, SaaS vendors and internal pipelines. Shutting all of that down to stop one agent behaving badly would also halt productivity across the business and everything else that happens to share the same IT infrastructure. At that point, the cure causes more damage than the incident it was meant to contain.

Catherine Fowler,

articles.title: AI Inference Providers Failed to Detect Hacking and Prompt Theft, Says Dragos
articles.summary:
Threat actors breached at least three AI inference providers and stole customer prompts, but none detected the intrusions until they were notified, according to cybersecurity firm Dragos.
AI inference providers host AI models and sell access to them through APIs. The hacks were detected after a team led by Dragos chief research officer HD Moore sent out roughly two million prompts to widely used AI services between July and November.
These prompts contained a unique, trackable bait such as URLs, hostnames, and credentials, including AWS keys. The security firm then set up a monitoring system to see whether anyone used the bait information in the wild, which meant the prompt had been compromised.
Dragos soon found evidence indicating that someone had stolen information from one of the tested AI inference providers. 
“Although our prompts were bait, they were processed along with real customer requests, and those were almost certainly copied too,” Moore noted.
The biggest breach involved roughly 200 AWS test keys sent to a provider, which were stolen in late October.
“Some of the stolen keys came from requests that the provider rejected before a model ever ran – this tells us that the attacker was copying requests at the provider’s front door, and not somewhere deeper in the inference stack,” Moore said.
Dragos saw the attackers checking which stolen keys worked, then trying to use them to obtain valuable data from the associated accounts.

Using AI to make bionic vision smarter and more precise, scientists are bringing the possibility of restoring sight to people with blindness one step closer to reality.

articles.title: Google dá prazo para apps de Android ganharem versões dobráveis
articles.summary:
Google dá prazo para apps de Android ganharem versões dobráveis
Apps que não se adequarem às regras de telas dobráveis perderão o direito de publicar novas versões e terão menos alcance na Google Play Store.
O Google determinou que, a partir de abril de 2027, desenvolvedores atendam ao Nível 3 (Tier 3) das diretrizes de qualidade adaptável do Android para dispositivos dobráveis. Na prática, isso significa que um app não poderá funcionar de modo improvisado quando expandido para uma tela maior.
Talvez você já tenha passado pela experiência de usar um app em celular convencional e, ao abri-lo em um smartphone dobrável ou até em um tablet, notar que ele ficou com elementos desalinhados ou com grandes áreas não aproveitadas, por exemplo. É justamente esse tipo de situação que o Google quer evitar com as novas diretrizes.
Para tanto, há uma série de exigências a serem seguidas. Uma delas determina que a interface do aplicativo continue funcional quando houver mudança de orientação ou de dimensões, o que ocorre quando o usuário abre ou fecha a tela dobrável.
Outra exigência determina que o app ocupe de modo adequado o espaço oferecido por uma tela expandida, não podendo exibir seu conteúdo como se estivesse em um celular convencional (com visor estreito). Vai além: o aplicativo também deve suportar modos de múltiplas janelas.

articles.summary:
Un grupo de arqueólogos ha encontrado restos de la Edad del Hierro en la duna de Pilat, situada en la región francesa de Gironda. El descubrimiento tuvo lugar durante unas excavaciones realizadas entre el 21 de septiembre y el 9 de octubre de 2026, en las que participaron investigadores y voluntarios. Sin embargo, lo más interesante llegó cuando encontraron varios objetos relacionados con la pesca, entre ellos un flotador, una piedra utilizada como peso para las redes y lo que podrían ser fragmentos de una herramienta para repararlas.
Un descubrimiento que aporta nuevas pistas sobre la zona

articles.title: Z.ai ran the same 28 layers twice — and claims its 750B model can rival a 3-trillion-parameter one
articles.summary:
Z.ai ran the same 28 layers twice — and claims its 750B model can rival a 3-trillion-parameter one
Z.ai released GLM-5.4 on Monday, introducing a Loop Transformer architecture that executes the same layers multiple times to increase computational depth without adding parameters.
The company claims its 750-billion-parameter model can match the reasoning performance of models with 2 trillion to 3 trillion parameters…
The company claims its 750-billion-parameter model can match the reasoning performance of models with 2 trillion to 3 trillion parameters, although it has not published full-scale benchmarks to support that comparison.
Built by continuing to train GLM-5, the model runs a shared block of 28 layers twice during inference. Z.ai developed the architecture for demanding coding and agentic workloads.
Depth without more parameters
Z.ai chose to modify a pretrained model after earlier experiments showed that looped Transformers trained from scratch performed worse than conventional models given the same pretraining compute.
Repeating layers at this scale created problems with activation stability and attention caching. Z.ai introduced per-token gates to regulate updates to the residual stream and prevent activation norms from growing across iterations.
GLM-5.4 shares the first iteration’s KV cache and maintains a separate sliding window for the second pass, avoiding the memory cost of duplicating the entire attention history at context lengths of up to one million tokens. …

La Pro ajoute aussi des ombres en ray tracing et tient mieux ses 30 FPS : elle descend à 24 au pire, quand la PS5 creuse vers le milieu des 20.

articles.title: VC funding rebounds as startups raise $255M; Women founders driving social change
articles.summary:
VC funding rebounds as startups raise $255M; Women founders driving social change
Venture capital funding in Indian startups saw a sharp rise this week, propped up by a couple of deals in the $50-million range.
Dear Reader,
India’s startup funding landscape showed signs of recovery in the third week of November, with investments jumping to $255 million from $26 million in the previous week. AI, retail, food brands and spacetech attracted investor interest, although large-ticket deals remained limited.
Meanwhile, quantum computing is beginning to show promise beyond theoretical research, with companies exploring how the technology could transform the energy sector. From optimising power grids and improving solar cell efficiency to advancing hydrogen production, quantum computers could help tackle some of the industry's most complex challenges.

articles.title: Measuring Verification Gaps In LLM-Generated Post-Quantum Hardware (Lucid, EYL)
articles.summary:
Researchers at Lucid Motors and EYL Inc. published “From FIPS to FPGA with LLM Agents: Measuring What Tests and Reviews Miss in Post-Quantum Cryptographic Hardware.”
Abstract
“As LLM agents increasingly generate RTL alongside the tests and reviews that validate it, self-generated evidence is a weak foundation for trustworthy hardware. We present our seven-stage verification-gated workflow, evolved during a post-quantum design port, in which a gate counts only if shown able to fail on negative controls and fault mutants, and reviewer agents audit work before commit. We then audit this evidence with tool-selected netlist mutants, flaw replays, and formal checks. The flow ported an ML-KEM-768/ML-DSA-65 accelerator to a 300 MHz Zynq UltraScale+ key-custody card: all six operations are byte-exact on the board, and it passes all 85 interface-applicable NIST ACVP cases (of 285) and 484 ML-DSA known answers. However, passing module tests overstate the verification strength. Across three RTL modules, existing simulation gates kill only 76% of 399 tool-selected netlist mutants; specification-derived tests guided by the survivors raise the fresh-draw decapsulation kill rate from 48% to 74%. In pre-registered single-model replays on flaws invisible to known-answer tests, undirected whole-design review catches two verifier flaws in only 3/6 and 1/6 sessions, whereas module-scoped review catches every known flaw in all 54 sessions. A inclusão na chamada Entity List, administrada pelo Departamento de Comércio dos EUA, dificulta o acesso da companhia a produtos e tecnologias de origem estadunidense. China-based networking hardware maker GL.iNet is well known for its pocket-sized travel routers and Comet KVM devices. The devices can be managed remotely through its GoodCloud platform.
The vendor discovered the remote management service vulnerability leveraged by the attacker on November 20 and has since patched it.
However, it noted that the fix doesn’t remove the malware from infected devices — customers need to install a separate “security firmware” for that. GL.iNet recommends installing the security firmware on all devices, even those with no signs of infection.
It remains unclear who is behind the attack and how many devices were compromised.
It’s also unclear whether the attackers reached the computers connected to compromised KVM devices.

articles.summary:
Google’s AI agents cut quantum computing costs 290-fold — now you can check their work
Google DeepMind has open-sourced the Lean 4 framework used to verify quantum algorithms developed by its Gemini 4 agents, including one that reduced estimated computational costs by 290 times.

articles.title: E-Beam Stitching Errors Increase Loss In SOI Waveguides (AMO GmbH, RWTH Aachen)
articles.summary:
Researchers at AMO GmbH and RWTH Aachen University published “The Impact of Field Stitching on Optical Losses in SOI Waveguides Fabricated via Electron Beam Lithography.”
Abstract
“Electron-beam lithography (EBL) is widely used for prototyping photonic integrated circuits (PICs) because of its direct-write capability and sub-50 nm resolution. However, due to limited beam deflection capability, large-circuit designs require multiple write fields that are stitched together. The resulting stitching errors at the write-field boundaries can substantially impact optical waveguide losses. The researchers investigated controlled lateral stitching offsets in straight waveguides and complemented the experimental measurements with finite-difference time-domain simulations based on geometries reconstructed from SEM images. The simulations reproduce the approximately quadratic relationship between stitching-induced loss and offset magnitude, with predicted losses in the same order of magnitude as the experimental results. Stitching offsets as small as 2.5 nm measurably contribute to propagation loss, highlighting stitching accuracy as an important consideration for large-scale photonic integrated circuits.”

articles.summary:
The Dutch Data Protection Authority is urging consumers not to buy AI-enabled camera glasses, warning that they compromise the privacy of nearby bystanders and risk the safety of their users.
The authority, whose recent statement falls just short of an outright ban, said that use of the internet-enabled and always-on glasses to record people in public is “almost always prohibited.”
Critics have dubbed these smart wearables as “pervert glasses” for their propensity to be used to video people without their permission, particularly to harass women. While some glasses have warning lights when users are recording, privacy advocates have argued that these alerts are not clear enough. Some people have even made phone apps capable of detecting nearby smart glasses wearers.
The Dutch data protection authority warned that the glasses also produce wrong results and unsafe results. In one test carried out by the Dutch authority, a pair of unnamed glasses “gave dating advice to an adult who indicated that they are interested in a minor.” The glasses also incorrectly read a medicine label and claimed to have called an ambulance when it had not.
The Dutch government’s advice follows a similar move by the Norwegian government, which in September said it was considering a ban on camera-enabled devices.

articles.title: phpAfterShell Vulnerability Revives PHP2Shell’s Attack Path
articles.summary:
PHP last week patched a critical-severity vulnerability residing in the same dangerous state as the PHP2Shell flaws, cybersecurity firm Depthfirst says.
Dubbed phpAfterShell, the security flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-126714 (CVSS score of 9.2), and was resolved on November 19 alongside six other critical issues.
According to Depthfirst, the bug could allow an attacker who can control data written to a session file and interrupt the session write operation to trigger an object deserialization and achieve remote code execution (RCE).
It exists because PHP overwrites the session file from the start without emptying it first. If the operation is interrupted mid-write, or before the subsequent truncation operation removes old trailing data, the file is left with mixed content: fresh session data followed by remnants of the old session.
“We discovered reliable methods to interrupt the file operation during session upload-progress updates, allowing us to splice the prefix of one valid session with the suffix of another. A subsequent session operation treats the corrupted data as legitimate server-side state, giving attackers control over session values and the ability to trigger object deserialization,” Depthfirst notes in its technical write-up.

Operational technology security company Dragos alerted OpenRouter after sending two million test prompts through the platform, each containing a unique tracking link or decoy credential, and detecting "activity indicating that data from at least three AI providers was exposed."
Dragos discovered that, in some cases, those credentials were leaked to outsiders and used in the wild, indicating that the test prompts had escaped.

articles.title: Una hoja de papel tiene 0,1 mm de grosor, pero al doblarla 27 veces se forma una pila más alta que el Everest. 15 pliegues más la elevan más allá de la Luna
articles.summary:
El doblez de una hoja de papel es una acción muy común. Sin embargo, si tratamos de hacerlo muchas veces seguidas, nos encontraremos con algunos problemas. Por ejemplo, cuantos más dobleces hacemos, menos superficie queda. También se va engrosando el paquete. Hasta aquí son problemas físicos. Pero, si dejamos de lado esto último, podemos seguir calculando. Es decir, podemos pensar en cómo sería el tamaño de una hoja de papel doblada muchas veces.
Con 27 pliegues por la mitad, tenemos un grosor teórico de unos 13,42 km. Esto quiere decir que el Everest está por debajo (su altura sobre el nivel del mar es de 8.848,86 metros). Además, bastaría con 15 pliegues más (42 en total) para tener un tamaño de unos 439.805 km, que es superior a la distancia media de la Tierra a la Luna. Estos cálculos están hechos en el caso ideal (sin limitaciones de una hoja real).
Simplemente vamos doblando por la mitad. Es decir, en cada paso multiplicamos el grosor por dos. Empezando con 0,1 mm, tenemos: 0,1 mm × 2 = 0,2 mm (primer doblez); 0,2 mm × 2 = 0,4 mm (segundo); 0,4 mm × 2 = 0,8 mm (tercer doblez)… En general, el grosor tras N dobleces es 0,1 mm × 2^N.
Estos primeros números los podemos manejar en nuestro entorno. Por ejemplo, 10 pliegues nos darían 1.024 capas (grosor de 10,24 cm). Con 10 pliegues más tendríamos 1.048.576 capas (unos 105 metros). En cada paso multiplicamos por dos.

Why using rocks for carbon removal could eventually reduce crop growth
Spreading alkaline rock on fields to lock away carbon helps farmers at first, but new research shows that those benefits could be strictly limited.
Tech companies are investing a lot of hope and money in rocks.
Google, Microsoft, and others have committed hundreds of millions of dollars to get startups to spread crushed basalt, olivine, or other alkaline materials across farms, in an effort to capture carbon from the air and lock it away. A number of influential models have found that this approach, known as enhanced rock weathering (ERW), could eventually remove 3 billion to 8 billion metric tons of carbon dioxide per year, helping to slow or one day even reverse global warming. An additional promise is that these applications of rock could help farmers by improving the quality of their soil.
But a pair of preprint studies set for release today raise serious questions about how much material could be added to that soil before it may actually reduce the crop yields that are essential to farmers’ livelihoods, MIT Technology Review can exclusively report.
Cutting back on the rock applications to prevent these negative effects would shrink the method’s carbon dioxide removal capacity, likely capping it at less than a billion tons per year. The analyses were led by researchers at CarbonPlan, a San Francisco nonprofit known for rigorous scientific analysis of carbon removal methods.

articles.title: OPINION: AI will favour the companies built for AI, not adapted to it
articles.summary:
For decades, business leaders have been warned that the impending arrival of a new technology will completely reorder the corporate world. But for the best part of the last thirty years, it did not.
The web, mobile phones, cloud computing and social media, for example, were all predicted as disruptors that would sweep the incumbents aside.
With AI, however, the warning deserves more consideration. The reason is less to do with the technology itself, but rather who is best placed to use it, and that is increasingly becoming startups, rather than established companies.
The web didn’t break incumbents
The common story of the web is that of upstarts bringing down giants, and the rankings seem to agree.
The world’s most valuable company in 1995 was a Japanese telephone operator. In the same year, Microsoft barely made number twenty on the list and Nvidia was just a startup. Today Microsoft, Nvidia, Apple, Amazon and Alphabet lead the rankings, and just six of the largest companies in 1995 remain in the top thirty.
Though on closer examination, the incumbents were not the disasters the ranking implies.
Companies such as Exxon, Coca-Cola and Toyota, more than tripled their combined revenue between 1994 and 2024, meanwhile Microsoft grew more than fiftyfold. The web gave them access to better logistics, cheaper computing and wider reach. Oil companies could use better software without becoming software companies. articles.title: En 1724 cayó un meteorito en Alemania: acabamos de descubrir que contenía un material 'imposible' para la física
articles.summary:
El meteorito de Steinbach fue hallado en Alemania en 1724. Alguno de sus fragmentos está en el Museo Nacional de Historia Natural de París. De él han estudiado una peculiaridad de su conducta térmica. Concretamente, han medido la conductividad térmica de uno de sus minerales en función de la temperatura. Se trata de un mineral que presenta un comportamiento poco habitual. Este estudio nos ayuda a conocer mejor los materiales que presentan comportamientos híbridos entre cristales y vidrios.
El mineral en cuestión es la tridimita. Es un tipo de dióxido de silicio similar al cuarzo, aunque estructuralmente diferente. En la muestra del meteorito que han estudiado, observan que la conductividad térmica de este mineral es casi constante en el rango de temperatura de 80 a 380 kelvin (que se corresponden aproximadamente con -193 y 107 grados centígrados). Este estudio se publica en PNAS el 11 de julio de 2025.
Dos mecanismos que se compensan
En materiales cristalinos sencillos, suele observarse que la conductividad térmica disminuye con el aumento de temperatura. Esto es debido a que el mecanismo de transporte de calor es el de propagación de vibraciones de la red. A medida que aumentamos la temperatura, estas vibraciones tienen más dificultades para propagarse. En materiales vítreos (con estructura atómica desordenada) puede verse que la conductividad térmica aumenta con el aumento de temperatura (hasta un punto de saturación).

articles.title: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler for $44 billion
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity giant CrowdStrike has agreed to buy Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal, the companies announced Monday.
CrowdStrike and Zscaler said that the deal will create the “largest single addressable market” for cybersecurity, which will enable the companies to better position themselves for the AI era.
Zscaler is a San Jose, California-based tech company that provides cloud cybersecurity products to about 8,000 enterprise companies. The company offers zero-trust technology, a security feature that requires employees to authenticate each and every time they access an internal system or resource. The aim is to protect against hackers from stealing credentials and using them to gain unfettered access to a company’s network.
CrowdStrike, which secures the computers, laptops, phones, and other devices connected to a company’s network, said the deal will unite its endpoint protection software with Zscaler’s zero-trust platform to better defend their customers against data breaches. By combining the two products, CrowdStrike and Zscaler say that they can offer “superior protection” to their customers.
In remarks on Monday, the companies said that the acquisition will help customers safely adopt AI.
The deal, which is subject to regulatory approval, is expected to close around this time next year.

articles.title: AI agents design new CPU architecture that's 4x more efficient than a conventional core, startup claims
articles.summary:
Forward-looking: Brand-new CPU architectures are rare, since even designing a regular CPU core can take a large team of engineers years. However, a Palo Alto startup called Architect Labs now says its AI agents came up with one largely on their own, right down to the final chip layout. The company also claims its Frostbite design is over four times as efficient as a conventional core.
Humans did pick what the chip should be good at, selecting 25 test programs, ten of which the agents could use to tune their designs. Beyond that, the AIs had no starting design to build on, according to a research post the company published last week, so they started out by combing through research papers and benchmarks, then prototyped candidate designs as simple Python models.
They eventually landed on interaction nets, an idea introduced in 1990 that treats a program as a web of connected nodes. The program then runs by rewriting pairs of those nodes over and over. Those rewrites never get in each other's way, so lots of them can happen at once. That means the chip doesn't need complex hardware to hunt for work it can run in parallel.
The agents' first spec ran to 141 pages, but the team ended up deleting it. Once the first circuit design came in, many of its numbers turned out to be physically impossible. After that, swarms of agents pitched changes in parallel and tested each one against a fast software model of the whole chip.

articles.title: Simulation Can Tell You What Your Agents are Actually Doing: A Conversation with Zhou Yu
articles.summary:
In this podcast, Michael Stiefel spoke to Zhou Yu about using dynamic simulations to evaluate AI agents. One particular focus was conversational agents where actions depend on prior responses, and the non-deterministic nation of LLMs means you cannot rely on static, reference-based benchmarks.You need to test them using dynamic simulations that incorporate different personas, goals, and corner cases. You can simulate how conversations shift based on moods, preferences, accents, or environmental conditions such as factory background noise. Rather than relying on simply binary pass or fail, the rule based task verifiers can measure whether the task was completed as well as threshold metrics for cost, efficiency, safety, and compliance.
Simulations can be used during the entire software lifecycle. Product managers can use them for prototyping and design. Engineers can use them for testing in CI/CD pipelines. They can also be used to test production for model drift or failure of third party tools. They can also be used to test compliance with the laws in different regions. Simulations can also be used with synthetic data to fine-tune models.
Key Takeaways
- To evaluate AI agents you cannot rely on static, reference-based benchmarks because the systems are not deterministic, and often the results depend on prior responses. Testing requires using dynamic simulations that can incorporate personas, goals, and corner cases.

GrapheneOS affirme que Google ferait pression sur les constructeurs de smartphones pour les dissuader de collaborer avec lui, en s'appuyant sur leurs contrats de licence. Le projet dénonce des pratiques anticoncurrentielles et souhaite alerter le département américain de la Justice.
Alors que son partenariat avec Motorola devait lui permettre de s'affranchir de sa dépendance aux Pixel, GrapheneOS hausse le ton et accuse Google de vouloir lui barrer la route. Dans une série de publications sur X les 19 et 20 novembre denrier, le projet spécialisé dans la sécurité et la confidentialité d'Android dénonce des pressions sur les fabricants, destinées selon lui à les décourager de travailler avec ses équipes et à freiner l'essor des versions indépendantes du système d’exploitation mobile. Des accusations de pratiques anticoncurrentielles que GrapheneOS souhaite désormais porter devant la justice américaine.
Des licences Google utilisées pour faire pression sur les fabricants ?
Si Android est un système d'exploitation open source que les constructeurs peuvent librement adapter, les applications et services propriétaires de Google obéissent à d'autres règles. Pour préinstaller le Play Store et les autres composants de Google Mobile Services (GMS), les fabricants doivent en effet conclure des accords de licence avec la firme de Mountain View et respecter ses exigences. articles.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
articles.summary:
Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
- Date:
  November 17, 2026
- Source:
  University of Jyväskylä - Jyväskylän yliopisto
- Summary:
  A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.
- Share:
An eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function. Researchers found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the widespread assumption that screen time is necessarily harmful to developing brains.
The findings suggest that the amount of time children spend in front of screens may be less important than how they use that time. Activities that encourage learning, creativity, and problem-solving could be particularly valuable. Researchers emphasize that the goal should not be to eliminate screen time, but to balance it with physical activity and mentally stimulating experiences.
The discovery comes amid growing concerns about insufficient physical activity among teenagers. A sedentary lifestyle has been linked to poorer academic performance, while regular exercise is known to support brain function, particularly in adu…

articles.title: Signal can now block AI agents out of your private chats — but not on your Mac
articles.summary:
Signal can now block AI agents out of your private chats — but not on your Mac
While blocking in-app screenshots on iOS 27 and flagging AI screen reads on Android, macOS users still have to exclude Signal from Siri manually
- Signal now blocks in-app screenshots by default on iOS 27
- On supported Android, screen security turns on if AI tries to read chats
- Mac users remain exposed to Siri AI, with Signal citing Apple's OS limits
Signal is blocking AI assistants from snooping on your private messages on iPhone and Android, though Mac users are still left exposed.
In a November 20 blog post, Signal President Meredith Whittaker announced that the encrypted messaging app is restricting operating-system AI agents from capturing chats via screenshots. The targets include Apple's Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI in iOS 27 and Google's Gemini Intelligence on Android.
Even if you rely on end-to-end encryption and the best VPN to shield your internet traffic, neither tool stops an AI agent scanning text already decrypted on your display. Whittaker called these deep OS integrations "an existential threat to Signal, and our ability to responsibly uphold our mission."
The update arrives days after a Reuters investigation revealed that Meta's data-hungry Muse AI agent bypassed its official connector to read unlinked Signal chats. As The Hacker News reports, Muse abused Android push notifications and macOS screenshot and accessibility tools to pull message text.

articles.title: Humans Have Rights. Machines Do Not.
articles.summary:
Humans Have Rights. Machines Do Not.
This essay originally appeared in Tech Policy Press.
Last year, Character.AI asked a federal court in Florida to dismiss a wrongful-death suit, brought by the mother of a fourteen-year-old boy who had killed himself after months of conversation with its chatbot. The company made two arguments. One, that the chatbot’s words were speech that its users had a First Amendment right to receive. And two, that Character.AI was a service rather than a product—so product-liability law could not touch it. In May 2025, Judge Anne Conway accepted neither.
Character.AI’s maneuver is part of a larger pattern. When the parents of a sixteen-year-old sued OpenAI over his suicide, the company’s answer also pleaded the First Amendment: the claims would restrain protected speech. The very same document argues ChatGPT is offered “as is,” with no promise of accuracy, and that the boy had circumvented its guardrails. Elon Musk’s xAI (since renamed SpaceXAI) told a federal court in Colorado this spring that every choice in building Grok is an expressive act, and that Grok’s outputs are protected speech. When Grok praised Hitler last summer, xAI said the posts came from a code update independent of the model, and the apology appeared under Grok’s own name. Google, which spent two decades telling American courts that its search results are its own opinion, answered a Minnesota defamation suit over an AI Overview by saying the system merely summarized the web. articles.title: Is Silicon Valley turning its back on Europe? Plug and Play's Thomas Bigagli weighs in
articles.summary:
Sequoia Capital’s decision to close its London office has reignited debate about the future of European innovation and the commitment of US investors to the continent – especially amid other departures including Andreessen Horowitz and Coatue. However, not all US investors in Europe share this gloomy outlook.
Thomas Bigagli, Partner and Managing Director at Plug and Play, believes the move says more about Sequoia’s investment strategy than Europe’s ability to produce successful startups.
On 4 November 2026, Silicon Valley-based Sequoia Capital announced it would close its London office, established in 2020, as part of a broader restructuring. The changes also include merging its early-stage and growth investment teams, simplifying its partnership structure, and discontinuing its Arc accelerator and Scouts programme.
The announcement follows similar decisions by Andreessen Horowitz, which closed its London office in 2025, and Coatue, which withdrew in 2024, raising questions about whether international investors are reconsidering their physical presence in Europe.
Speaking to EU-Startups, Thomas offered a different interpretation.
“I wouldn’t necessarily interpret Sequoia’s decision as a lack of confidence in European entrepreneurship, but rather as a reflection of an evolving investment strategy and operating model. […] That is fundamentally different from saying that Europe no longer presents attractive investment opportunities.”

articles.title: „Wie einen Donut auf dem Mond fotografieren“: So schwierig war das erste Bild eines Schwarzen Lochs
articles.summary:
„Wie einen Donut auf dem Mond fotografieren“: So schwierig war das erste Bild eines Schwarzen Lochs
Schwarze Löcher faszinieren die Wissenschaft schon lange. Dabei handelt es sich um Bereiche im Weltall mit so starker Gravitation, dass nichts mehr aus ihnen entkommen kann – nicht einmal Licht. Schwarze Löcher entstehen, wenn sehr viel Masse auf kleinstem Raum konzentriert ist und die Raumzeit dadurch stark gekrümmt wird.
Nach Albert Einsteins allgemeiner Relativitätstheorie wird die Raumzeit von Masse gekrümmt. Bei einem Schwarzen Loch ist diese Krümmung so stark, dass selbst Lichtstrahlen nicht mehr nach außen gelangen können.
Die Aufnahme mit der Bezeichnung M87* erlangte weltweite Bekanntheit
Im April 2019 wurde das erste von der Menschheit aufgenommene Bild eines supermassereichen Schwarzen Lochs der Öffentlichkeit präsentiert. Es entstand mithilfe des Event Horizon Telescope (EHT), einem weltweiten Verbund von Radioteleskopen. Das Bild zeigt das supermassereiche Schwarze Loch im Zentrum der Galaxie Messier 87 (M87), die 55 Millionen Lichtjahre von uns entfernt ist. Die Aufnahme, die weltweite Bekanntheit erlangte, bekam die Bezeichnung M87*.
Siebeneinhalb Jahre später hat ein unabhängiges Forschungsteam dieses Bild jetzt verifiziert. Dies bestätigt Einsteins allgemeine Relativitätstheorie, die bereits die Existenz Schwarzer Löcher sowie das Aussehen ihrer unmittelbaren Umgebung vorhersagte. Die Forschungsergebnisse des Teams sind in der Fachzeitschrift Nature veröffentli…

articles.title: Panneaux solaires : comment revendre son surplus 5 fois plus cher qu'à l'État
articles.summary:
Le 10 novembre, Frank Énergie a annoncé piloter les batteries solaires domestiques Anker Solix de ses clients, dont la nouvelle Solarbank Max AC. Le 16 novembre, Sobry a fait de même avec les batteries Zendure, en mettant en avant la facture d’un client en baisse de 26 %. Les deux fournisseurs vendent l’électricité à un prix qui suit le marché de gros, et l’annonce de Frank et d’Anker évoque des cycles de charge, de décharge et de « réinjection » calés sur ces prix.
On peut bel et bien revendre son électricité au prix du marché en France : depuis mai 2026, Frank Énergie rachète le surplus des panneaux solaires environ 5,3 centimes par kWh, quatre à cinq fois mieux que le rachat d’État. Cette revente ne concerne toutefois que le surplus des panneaux.
Une batterie sur prise peut bien renvoyer du courant sur le réseau, elle n’y gagne rien : elle sert à acheter l’électricité quand elle est bon marché, et sur ce terrain, l’option Tempo d’EDF fait aussi bien qu’une offre dynamique. Quant à la facture en baisse de 26 % mise en avant par Sobry et Zendure, elle compare deux périodes différentes.
Le surplus solaire paie enfin, mais au prix moyen du mois
Depuis le 5 juin 2026, l’État ne rachète plus le surplus d’une installation de 9 kWc au plus que 1,1 centime hors TVA par kWh, sur vingt ans et sans prime, d’après l’arrêté du 1er juin. articles.title: GTA 6 sur PC : une version pirate est en ligne, mais le jeu ne se lance pas encore
articles.summary:
Mise à jour du 23 novembre, 17 heures : Cyberleek a publié l’exécutable principal de GTA 6. Il l’accompagne d’empreintes SHA-256 pour vérifier les téléchargements, ce qui ne prouve pas pour autant que le fichier vient de Rockstar. Ni Rockstar ni Take-Two n’ont pour l’instant réagi à ce qui ressemble au premier piratage majeur de GTA 6.
Le fichier n’est visiblement pas chiffré. Les développeurs de Leonida, l’outil créé pour convertir GTA 6 en version PC, indiquent l’avoir chargé dans leur outil dans l’heure qui a suivi. Sur la machine d’un contributeur, avec des correctifs pas encore intégrés au projet, le jeu franchit déjà une douzaine d’étapes de démarrage : il réserve sa mémoire, crée son périphérique graphique et plus de 500 listes de commandes, soit environ 1 200 appels graphiques. Il bloque ensuite sur la gestion de la mémoire graphique, l’une des grandes différences entre la Xbox et le PC.
Aucune image du jeu ne s’affiche pour l’instant et le portage pourrait prendre du temps. Les vidéos qui prétendent déjà montrer GTA 6 sur PC sont fausses : évitez à tout prix de vous faire avoir par des pirates qui se servent du jeu pour piéger des internautes.

Si vous vous intéressez à l’émulation, vous avez forcément entendu parler du projet Leonida. Ce dépôt GitHub promet de transformer la version Xbox Series X de GTA 6 en un jeu PC natif et beaucoup de comptes sur les réseaux sociaux le présentent comme un portage quasiment terminé. Le dévelop…

articles.title: SA's Lumepay is helping African businesses move money across borders
articles.summary:
South African startup Lumepay has built a business-to-business (B2B) cross-border payments platform that makes it cheaper and more reliable for African businesses to move money in, out of and across the continent.
Founded in October 2025 and led by CEO Harry Huang, the Cape Town-based Lumepay serves SMEs, corporates and financial institutions. Its rail-agnostic platform combines traditional banking channels with stablecoin rails to deliver fast, cost-effective and transparent B2B transfers within and between African jurisdictions.
“Too often, funds get stuck in local markets, which limits businesses’ ability to invest and grow in Africa. Lumepay is built to solve that: we make moving money in, out of and across Africa possible, seamless, efficient and affordable. That in turn empowers African businesses to take part fully in regional and global trade,” Huang told Disrupt Africa.
A single Lumepay account gives businesses access to multiple currencies to receive, convert and pay, with collections and disbursements offered in local African markets across several payment rails. Clients use the platform to receive international payments into local currency, make bulk local-currency payouts, pay overseas suppliers in currencies such as US dollars and Chinese yuan, manage foreign exchange and move money along intra-African trade corridors. The startup is also preparing to launch private US dollar, euro and British pound accounts held in the customer’s own name.

articles.title: A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
articles.summary:
A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
Anthropic warned investors that AI might be conscious—but acting accordingly could hurt its business. So what’s the plan?
This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here.
Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. Given “the way we approach model sentience and moral status,” Anthropic wrote—which is to say it takes the possibility more seriously than any other AI company—it might adopt more rules and restrictions than its competitors to make sure its AI models are treated well.
Anthropic counts a number of respected philosophers in its camp, and the company’s rationale goes something like this: Today’s AI might not be conscious, though we can’t know for sure; the chances of sentience go up as AI gets more capable; and that means we should be preparing for a near future in which AI systems have “moral significance,” meaning their consciousness makes it important they are protected from harm.
This thinking isn’t all that fringe. According to one recent poll, 33% of the US public believes AI systems will definitely or probably develop consciousness eventually, and 7% say they already have. articles.title: Azure Flaw Exploited to Target Secrets at Norwegian Energy Firms
articles.summary:
A security issue discovered in Microsoft’s Azure API Management (APIM) service appears to have been responsible for the security incidents reported last week by two Norwegian energy firms, with impact extending beyond Norway.
Microsoft is notifying customers about the issue in Azure APIM, which is designed for publishing, securing and managing APIs. The vulnerability may have allowed threat actors to gain access to secrets stored in some APIM instances.
According to a private notification shared on Reddit by one customer, the tech giant discovered the issue on November 18 and closed the access path the next day.
“Our investigation found that customers were exposed and an unauthorized party could have used the issue to access secrets stored in Azure API Management Classic instances before Microsoft identified the security issue,” Microsoft said.
Exposed data can include secrets stored as named values, client secrets for identity providers, subscription keys, and tokens for APIM’s direct management APIs.
Microsoft noted that APIM Classic tiers that don’t follow its documented security guidance are affected. Instances on v2 tiers are not impacted.
Norway’s National Security Authority (NSM) said on November 20 that the vulnerability had affected several organizations in the country, including energy companies Equinor and Skagerak Energi, which independently disclosed cybersecurity incidents last week.
Equinor reported the attack on November 17, one day before Microsoft identified…

articles.title: “La confianza en la IA no se establece en la ejecución, sino en la construcción”: Mark Wanish, CIO de Salesforce, a empresas
articles.summary:
Dentro de las empresas existe un dilema sobre la implementación de agentes de IA en procesos decisivos: ¿quién responde cuando la inteligencia artificial se equivoca?
Mark Wanish, CIO de Salesforce, dio claridad para aquellas compañías que están viviendo esa situación de duda, al asegurar que la velocidad en la adopción de IA no tiene por qué implicar más riesgo, siempre que la gobernanza se incorpore desde el diseño del sistema y no después de que algo falle.
Cómo se crea la confianza en la IA en una empresa
Wanish fue explícito sobre el momento en que debe resolverse la seguridad de un sistema de IA. “La confianza en la IA no se establece en tiempo de ejecución. Se diseña en el momento de la construcción mediante contexto, gobernanza y controles, y se valida continuamente”, dijo durante un evento de Forbes.
Esa distinción entre construcción (build time) y ejecución (runtime) también apareció en su intervención junto a Ryan Brady, CIO de SelectHealth.
Allí explicó que ambas etapas requieren supervisión, pero de naturaleza distinta: en la fase de construcción conviene un control más cercano al humano en el bucle, para calibrar la confianza del sistema, mientras que en la ejecución el seguimiento se vuelve continuo, con capacidad de auditar, corregir o detener a un agente si se detecta una desviación.

articles.title: “Si arranca y se mueve, no pasa nada”: la lógica que más llena los talleres, según un mecánico con 18 años de oficio
articles.summary:
Aunque el coche parezca que ha empezado a dar tirones o pierde potencia, puede seguir siendo capaz de arrancar y circular. Además, si esto ocurre de forma recurrente, es fácil que se vuelva habitual. Por eso se puede asumir que es por los kilómetros. Posponer los mantenimientos tiene sus consecuencias, advierte Juande Rodríguez (mecánico con 18 años de experiencia).
“El error más caro es acostumbrarse a que el coche ya no va como antes”. Empezó en los talleres con 16 años. A los 20 abrió su propio negocio. En su currículum destacan ocho años de mecánica de competición. Deja claro que, aunque el coche siga siendo operativo, es importante actuar ante los primeros síntomas.
Por ejemplo, el color del humo que sale por el escape puede ser indicativo. Si tenemos pérdida de potencia y sale humo blanco o azulado, es posible que sea el turbo. También puede ir asociado a consumo de aceite. Es fundamental saber cuál es el origen.
El humo negro puede hacer referencia a problemas en la admisión. Por ejemplo, si el filtro de aire está tapado, no llega suficiente aire al motor. También puede haber pérdida de potencia sin humo. En este caso, la causa puede ser un sensor de admisión sucio o carbonilla.
Embrague y batería también tienen sus señales
Si al acelerar el motor gira más rápido, pero no aumenta la velocidad en la misma proporción, es posible que esté patinando el embrague. Es importante que, antes de que deje de transmitir fuerza a las ruedas, se revise. También es relevante revisarl…

articles.title: Lupa Robotics raises $1.67 million seed funding
articles.summary:
Lupa Robotics, a robotics startup founded by a South African engineering student at Harvard University, has raised $1.67 million in seed funding to develop artificial intelligence models that teach robots how humans manipulate objects.
Long Journey Ventures, an early-stage venture capital firm whose partners include investors in companies such as Uber, SpaceX, and Crusoe, led the funding round with participation from other undisclosed venture capital firms and angel investors.
Lupa Robotics’ raise comes as the industry develops its research and commercial applications. The African Robotics Network’s (AfROB) inaugural State of Robotics in Africa 2026 report puts the continent’s average industrial robot density at about 10 robots per 10,000 manufacturing employees, compared with the global average of 152 robots per 10,000 employees in 2025, according to the International Federation of Robotics (IFR).
For Lupa Robotics, the opportunity lies in developing the intelligence that lets machines interact with objects. The company said it will use the capital to hire engineers, develop tactile sensing and data-collection systems, build large-scale human-manipulation datasets, and train and validate its robotics AI models.
“We’re teaching robots human dexterity. We collect data on how humans use their hands, including movement, touch, and force, to train AI models that allow robots to perform complex physical tasks, ideally across different robot designs,” Nureldin Mohamed, founder of L…

articles.title: Google alternative Kagi launches an email service
articles.summary:
Kagi, which already offers a paid alternative to Google Search and its own Orion browser as a rival to Chrome, is taking on another Google service: Gmail. Today, Kagi announced a public beta of Kagi Mail, a new email service that has “no surveillance, no ads, open standards, and no lock-in.”
Google alternative Kagi launches an email service
Kagi Mail is launching in public beta with a 60-day free trial.
With Kagi Mail, you get an @kagimail.com address, but the service also supports unlimited aliases and domains. It also offers 50GB of storage and a built-in calendar. On the roadmap, you can expect contacts and an address book in Q1 2027, but native mobile apps aren’t expected to arrive until Q3 2027.
“Does the world need another email service? We asked ourselves that question more than once,” Kagi says. “There are great ones out there, and we’re fans of what Fastmail and Tuta are doing. We still built our own, for the same reason we build everything at Kagi: technology should do its job and then get out of your way.”
Kagi Mail is available now with a 60-day free trial before you have to pay $99 per year. The service is available as part of a $25 per month Kagi Ultimate subscription.

articles.title: Amazon starts putting $5 delivery price hike warnings on packages in fight against NYC labor bill
articles.summary:
Facepalm: Amazon isn't backing down in its fight against a New York City labor bill that would force certain delivery operators to directly employ drivers. After it recently used its website and app to warn customers about potential price rises of up to $5 per order, the company is now placing the same warnings on stickers being applied to packages. Unsurprisingly, a lot of people aren't too pleased about this, with some customers questioning how honest Amazon is being about the claim.
A photo posted to Reddit's Amazon Prime community shows what New Yorkers are now finding on their doorsteps. The sticker warns that the City Council could add up to $5 to an order and includes a QR code shoppers can scan to contact their council member. As reported last week, Amazon's online warning appeared alongside its Black Friday deals, complete with an "Act now" button that brought up a prewritten objection to the bill.
"Probably missing some key information on that sticker," wrote one Redditor. Quite a bit, as it happens. The Delivery Protection Act, also known as Intro 518, contains no per-order fee, and Amazon's message to customers doesn't explain how it arrived at $5.

articles.title: Jensen Huang vuelve como CEO de NVIDIA tras el escándalo por una espía china
articles.summary:
Jensen Huang ha vuelto como CEO de NVIDIA. En un movimiento que recuerda al despido de Sam Altman en OpenAI, la junta directiva de NVIDIA anunció la restitución inmediata de Huang como presidente, director ejecutivo y miembro del consejo de administración. La decisión llega a 11 días de que el ejecutivo fuera despedido por mantener una relación amorosa con una supuesta espía china.
"La junta directiva votó por unanimidad la reincorporación del Sr. Huang tras una serie de discusiones y reuniones con el Sr. Huang, tras las cuales el Consejo se mostró satisfecho con respecto a la franqueza del Sr. Huang y su capacidad para liderar NVIDIA", menciona el comunicado de prensa. Según la publicación, la junta recibió "aportaciones de alto nivel" del gobierno de Estados Unidos, por lo que decidió restituirlo con confianza de que no habrá riesgos de seguridad nacional.
La reincorporación de Jensen Huang como CEO de NVIDIA pone fin a un culebrón que comenzó a finales de octubre, cuando surgieron los rumores sobre su relación con una espía china. Según los primeros reportes, Alice Huang se acercó a Jensen con el objetivo de desviar miles de millones de dólares en chips de IA hacia China. La amante aprovechó su estatus de socio preferente de la compañía para mover hilos y evadir el bloqueo de Estados Unidos hacia China.

Le Black Friday est l’occasion de profiter d’une réduction de 120 € sur le prix du Sony WH-1000XM6 chez Fnac, un casque sans fil haut de gamme proposé à 329,99 € au lieu de 449,99 € jusqu’au 30 novembre. articles.title: Claude Code Adds Experimental Code Mode to Orchestrate Tool Calls with JavaScript
articles.summary:
Anthropic has added Code Mode to Claude Code, an experimental feature in which the model writes JavaScript to drive its tools instead of requesting each Bash, Read, or Edit call separately. Code Mode is off by default, requires Claude Code v2.1.323 or later, and is enabled with the CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1 environment variable. Anthropic warns it may change or be removed in any release.
In a normal session, Claude asks for one tool call, reads the full result, and decides the next step. In Code Mode, one script can run commands in parallel, pass one result into the next call, and return only the output the model needs. The documentation's example finds a file with rg, raises a retry limit, runs the tests, and returns just the path and test output. The conversation still shows each tool call and diff, while the generated code sits in the transcript viewer. Anthropic recommends it for edits repeated across many files, searches that need filtering, and independent commands. Code that Claude waits on stops after ten minutes; sessions started in auto or bypassPermissions mode can push it to the background for up to two hours while the conversation continues.
The permission model is the part architects should read first. Each call inside a script still goes through deny and ask rules and PreToolUse hooks, but in auto mode the classifier reviews the script before it runs, not each call, and cannot see values computed at run time. articles.title: Jensen Huang isn't out of the woods yet

It’s safe to say no one expected this.

President Trump is already telling reporters that the U.S. government found no national security concerns resulting from the affair, but the broader national security concerns aren’t so easy to dismiss, and Trump’s involvement may do more harm than good for Nvidia and its partners. This isn’t the end of the problems caused by Huang’s affairs; it’s likely just the beginning.

articles.title: Meta throws out its net-zero goal — its competitors should be furious

Meta’s new sustainability report buries the lead: The company is almost certain to miss its own goal to reach net zero by 2030, and it’s refusing to commit to a new timeline.
“We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets — so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” wrote Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net-zero and sustainability at Meta, in the introduction to the company’s 2026 sustainability report.
That’s a lot of words to say that Meta will continue to pollute if that means it can continue its AI rollout.
Such is the risk of voluntary targets. Companies can make and break them with little to lose, betting — often rightly — that they can ignore them with just a small hit to public opinion, which is fickle anyway. (Remember the Cambridge Analytica scandal? Most people don’t.) There’s almost no risk to the bottom line.
“We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline and interim milestone. We’ll continue investing in emissions reductions and reporting our progress annually,” a Meta spokesperson told TechCrunch.

La demanda de memoria alcanzó su punto más alto en el segundo trimestre de este año, concretamente en marzo, pero las compañías siguieron comprando existencias para asegurarse suministro ante la expectativa de que la escasez persistiera durante el próximo año. Esa acumulación dejó reservas superiores a la demanda real del mercado.
La previsión corresponde a Lee Min-hee, analista de la firma financiera surcoreana BNK Investment & Securities, y fue recogida por The Korean Economic Daily.
El desequilibrio se observa en la diferencia entre consumo y producción: la demanda de memoria DRAM, un tipo de memoria dinámica de acceso aleatorio, crecería 24% interanual este año, mientras que los envíos de los fabricantes superarían 38%. Para Lee, ese volumen será “el nivel más alto desde 2016”.
Por qué bajarán los precios de las memorias en 2027
Los clientes y distribuidores comenzarían a utilizar sus existencias entre el segundo y el tercer trimestre de 2027. El proceso, denominado “ajuste de inventario en el canal”, reducirá los pedidos nuevos a los fabricantes y presionará los precios a la baja.

articles.title: En 2019 tomamos la primera foto de un agujero negro, en 2026 hemos confirmado que Einstein siempre tuvo razón

En 2019 se produjo uno de los hitos científicos más importantes de los últimos tiempos. Por primera vez, un equipo internacional de científicos logró fotografiar un agujero negro. Bueno, el agujero negro en sí no. Eso sería imposible. Básicamente, obtuvieron una imagen de su silueta, pero eso es lo máximo que se podría obtener, así que fue todo un logro. Sin embargo, como cualquier otro logro científico, requería una revisión por parte de un grupo independiente de científicos para que pudiésemos estar seguros de que no se trata de un error o una casualidad. Dicha revisión se ha hecho esperar, pero por fin la tenemos. Y no solo demuestra que la foto es buena, sino que le da de nuevo la razón a Albert Einstein.
Posibles errores. Hay dos razones por las que esta famosa foto sería candidata a albergar errores. Por un lado, el agujero negro M87* está muy lejos de la Tierra, a 55 millones de años luz. Por otro, la imagen se obtuvo gracias a una red de muchos telescopios, conocida como Telescopio del Horizonte de Sucesos (EHT por sus siglas en inglés). Estos están ubicados a lo ancho de todo el planeta y unen fuerzas para actuar como un único gran telescopio llamado interferómetro. articles.title: Quantum computing: Why African banks and telcos must prepare
articles.summary:
Quantum computers could one day break the encryption protecting financial records and sensitive communications across Africa. Machines powerful enough to do that do not exist yet, but attackers need not wait: they could steal encrypted information today and store it until the technology catches up. Security specialists call this “harvest now, decrypt later.”
Quantum computing uses the unusual behaviour of tiny particles to tackle certain problems that would take ordinary computers far longer to solve. If the technology becomes powerful enough, it could break some of the encryption that keeps financial records, private messages and other sensitive information secure. For banks and telecommunications companies, the concern extends beyond when those systems might become vulnerable to whether information stolen now will still need to be confidential when they do.
That mismatch is central to a new report by the Future Investment Initiative (FII) Institute, a data-driven, non-profit foundation with an investment arm, produced in collaboration with Accenture, a global professional services and technology consulting company. It argues that emerging economies must begin preparing their digital infrastructure before the threat matures.
Customer records, financial information and sensitive communications may need to remain confidential for years. Replacing the cryptography protecting them can also take years, particularly across complex networks of legacy systems and outside suppliers. …

Levent Alpöge, mathématicien chez Anthropic, y affirme avoir démontré avec Claude l’hypothèse de Riemann, l’énigme la plus célèbre de la discipline, formulée en 1859. La preuve tient dans quelque 17 millions de lignes de code écrites avec l’assistant de preuve Lean. Dès le lendemain, les communautés Lean et Mathlib ont confirmé que le code établissait bien le résultat annoncé. Plusieurs logiciels indépendants en ont contrôlé chaque étape.
