Mais son texte est surtout un avertissement : l’année qui vient sera décisive, et la société ne doit pas « passer la main » à l’IA.
Côté mathématiques, pourtant, l’histoire ne fait que commencer. La preuve a été vérifiée par ordinateur, mais en comprendre les idées est un autre chantier. À l’université de Waterloo, le mathématicien Michael Rubinstein a demandé à trois modèles d’IA de reconstituer le raisonnement à partir du code : leur document de travail n’en explique encore qu’une partie. A GeForce driver is an incredibly complex piece of software, We have an army of software engineers constantly adding features and fixing bugs. These changes are checked into the main driver branches, which are eventually run through a massive QA process and released.

This process has served us pretty well over the years but it has one significant weakness. Researchers at the University of Plymouth have now developed an artificial intelligence system that could help doctors identify people at risk of bladder cancer years before they receive a diagnosis. In some patients, the technology detected subtle warning signals dating back as far as five years.

Amazon has agreed to acquire a good chunk of Israeli startup Decart.
The e-commerce and cloud giant is paying $7.5 billion for the startup, according to Bloomberg.
Decart has made a name for itself building interactive real-time world models — most recently Oasis 3 — and AI video-generation tools. But under the hood, the company stands out for its Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), software that helps AI models run efficiently on Nvidia, Amazon, and Google’s hardware.
As part of the deal, Amazon will acquire the technology behind DOS, as well as Decart’s founding team and team of AI researchers and engineers, Amazon said in a blog post.
“Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip,” said Peter DeSantis, SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, quantum computing, at Amazon. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost.”
Amazon, which has so far been using its Trainium chips at its own data centers, is preparing to start selling them to customers as a competitor to Nvidia. Decart’s technology could make it easier for customers to run their workloads on Amazon chips, rather than Nvidia’s, which has been the gold standard so far.
Decart and Amazon did not immediately return requests for comment.

articles.title: OPINION: Europe's rearmament risks creating empty factories
articles.summary:
Weapons factories are springing up all over Europe as proof, many say, that the continent is taking its rearmament seriously. It seems so simple. Build factories, manufacture arms and kit, and Europe, faced with aggression on its eastern flank and the changing realities of a complex, multipolar world, will be able to take care of itself and its interests after decades of low defence investment.
Of course, it is not so simple. Because supply chains, the networks of production and distribution on which all manufacturing relies, are not all in Europe, and do not scale in proportion to manufacturing.
To think that they do is to believe, wrongly, that a company may get funding, massively improve its production capacity, and never have to worry that a chip, or some unusual component, might stop it from manufacturing anything.
Factories do not exist in isolation: they rest on broad industrial foundations, the absence of which means they cannot deliver. Hence Europe cannot both rebuild its defence industry and let its wider industrial base atrophy. To ramp up military manufacturing is also to ramp up manufacturing as such.
The industrial policy question
The question, then, relates not to whether Europe has enough factories. Indeed, weapons factories are expanding at three times the rate they did in peacetime, covering some 7 million square metres of new industrial development, but whether Europe is pursuing the right industrial policy.

Las Vegas welcomed Formula 1 to its streets this past weekend. And for the first time since the event’s inception in 2023, the Grand Prix delivered on a long-promised spectacle. The racing was closer to an IndyCar oval race than anything F1 fans will have seen since slipstreaming was the order of the day at places like Monza and Hockenheim, back when humans were still landing on the Moon and downforce had yet to fundamentally change racing.
The Vegas street circuit—the one that looks like an upside-down pig—is an extreme outlier on the calendar. It has plenty of long straights, so this year’s cars still suffer from energy starvation throughout the lap, as the inadequate size of their lithium-ion hybrid batteries means they become depleted very quickly, leaving the cars on just over half power with their V6 engines operating without the benefit of the hybrid’s electric motor.
And because it takes place at night, in the desert, in November, it’s cold—much, much colder than anywhere else the sport will visit all year. This coming weekend in the Middle East, track temperatures may well exceed 122° F (50° C ); on Saturday night in Nevada the track was a mere 59° F (15° C). Combined with the concrete streets, that spells low grip, but there is an added benefit—virtually no tire wear or overheating.
FP1 was completely rained out. A few drivers completed installation laps, but the risk of a crash was far too high.

articles.title: Netflix at QConSF 2026: Retrofitting the SDLC for AI Coding Agents

At QCon San Francisco 2026, Mark Khuzam, senior software engineer at Netflix, described how the company's Commerce team retrofitted its software development lifecycle so that AI coding agents and engineers could ship together safely.
Khuzam argued that most of the work was not about agents at all, but about documentation, consistency and review.
Much of Commerce runs as server-driven UI, an approach Netflix has discussed at QCon before. A single screen-composition service behind the API gateway builds screens for iOS, Android, web and TV.
Khuzam opened with a mock company email announcing that every engineer now had Claude Code and asking how much faster everyone was shipping. The problem the team ran into next was summed up in one line.
Agents promised speed. But we spent 20 years building for humans.
The team's first attempt was having an agent migrate tests, and it took four tries. The team started with "migrate this file," then added instructions, then the APIs to use, then how to mock data.
The docs were also hard to find, since the agent's context window ran out before it found the right page. And they were inconsistent, because tests were not written the same way across the codebase.
Developers rated the internal framework at a Net Promoter Score of -3. Moving from one test to a whole feature, from screen to data to route to test, meant teaching the agent how the team builds.

articles.title: COP31 ends in failure as countries split over fossil fuels, climate finance

ANTALYA, Turkey—By the time the United Nations COP31 climate talks ended Sunday afternoon, the conference center resembled a going-out-of-business sale at a pawnshop for broken dreams.
As cleaning crews cleared away the debris left by more than 100,000 participants, Murat Kurum, president of the Conference of the Parties and Turkey’s minister of environment, urbanization, and climate change, tried to tie together disparate parts of a draft climate deal with a shiny ribbon of multilateralism.
Many countries were not buying it.
For the first time since 2009, the conference ended without consensus on a cover decision, the concluding statement that typically signals global solidarity on how to confront the worsening climate crisis. Countries did adopt several decisions, including a program to help workers and communities transition away from fossil fuels, and a plan to assess progress on climate adaptation.
The failure to agree on an overarching conference statement reflected deep divisions over whether the agreement should mention fossil fuels and carbon capture, as well as how much climate financing developed countries should provide to developing nations hit by costly climate disasters.
The European Union, as well as several Latin American countries and Pacific Island states, said they would not accept the proposed text from the conference leaders.

Tesla en tire des vidéos promotionnelles et Elon Musk les relaie avec gourmandise. Des seniors américains achètent une Tesla pour son option de conduite assistée, facturée 99 dollars par mois, parce qu'ils ne se sentent plus capables de conduire. articles.title: Un telescopio en Sudáfrica captó una señal láser procedente de más de 8.000 millones de años luz, y los astrónomos saben de dónde viene
articles.summary:
El radiotelescopio MeerKAT de Sudáfrica ha detectado una especie de láser natural que emite en ondas de radio desde una galaxia a más de 8.000 millones de años luz. El descubrimiento fue publicado en febrero de 2026 por el Instituto Interuniversitario de Astronomía Intensiva en Datos (IDIA), y los astrónomos ya saben de dónde procede la señal y por qué ha llegado con tanta fuerza.
Un láser que emite en radio. El origen está en el gas de hidroxilo de las galaxias, que puede producir una emisión máser muy intensa, parecida a la de un láser pero en longitudes de onda de radio. Y cuando esa emisión se vuelve excepcionalmente potente, los astrónomos hablan de un megamáser. Vamos, que es un láser cósmico, aunque invisible para nuestros ojos.
Son fenómenos poco frecuentes que funcionan como balizas cósmicas y revelan información importante sobre las galaxias del universo primitivo.
Una lupa en mitad del camino. “Este sistema es verdaderamente extraordinario”, asegura Thato Manamela, investigador posdoctoral de la Universidad de Pretoria con financiación del Observatorio Radioastronómico de Sudáfrica (SARAO) y autor principal del estudio sobre el descubrimiento.
Y es que la señal no viajó sola, tal y como explica (traducción propia del inglés): “Estamos viendo el equivalente en radio de un láser a medio universo de distancia. articles.title: Si la pregunta es cómo podemos saber que una solución matemática es correcta sin entenderla, la respuestiene cuatro letras: Lean

En 1998, Thomas Hales y Samuel Ferguson dieron por demostrada la conjetura de Kepler, un viejo problema que pregunta sobre si hay una forma más compacta de apilar esferas que la que usan los fruteros con las naranjas. Su respuesta era que no, pero no todo el mundo estaba de acuerdo con ellos.
El asunto se polarizó tanto que, tras cuatro años de revisión, un panel de doce árbitros de Annals of Mathematics se declaró "99 % seguro" de que la prueba era correcta. Y ni siquiera esto, pese a la victoria que suponía para los dos matemáticos, acabó con el debate.
Fue entonces cuando Hales se dio cuenta de que la única forma de cerrar el asunto era que lo comprobara una máquina. Parecía fácil, pero no lo era. Anunció el proyecto de Flyspeck en enero de 2003, pero no lo terminó hasta agosto de 2014.
Era un sistema con problemas. Pero abrió un mundo de posibilidades. Hoy por hoy, como acaba de recordarnos la hipótesis de Riemann, esa idea de Hales se ha convertido en una pieza básica de la matemática del futuro. Lo único es que esa idea está encarnada ahora en Lean.
¿Lean? En 2015, Leonardo de Moura hizo público un demostrador de código abierto "con un núcleo de confianza pequeño": Lean. Era el último paso de un viaje que había iniciado una década antes en Microsoft desarrollando resolutores automáticos de problemas lógicos. En último término, la idea de Hales era sencillamente eso: comprobar que una prueba respetaba las reglas lógicas que debía cumplir.

articles.title: JEP 545 Moves ZGC Memory Preparation off the Startup Path in JDK 28
articles.summary:
JEP 545, Faster Startup and Warmup with ZGC, has been integrated into JDK 28, moving the work of acquiring and preparing heap memory off the startup path and onto dedicated concurrent worker threads. On Linux 6.1 and later it also upgrades 4 KB pages to 2 MB pages while the application runs. The 2 MB initial heap behind the JEP's headline numbers comes from elsewhere: adaptive heap sizing, in the companion JEP 546, which still defaults to off.
Deploying ZGC has until now meant choosing which half of a trade-off to pay for. The collector's pause times do not grow with the heap, but its collection frequency does, so a small heap brings on early and frequent cycles. The JEP describes the older ergonomic behavior of committing one sixty-fourth of physical memory for the initial heap.
A team chasing fast startup set a tiny -Xms and accepted a long warmup, because the collector then had to acquire and prepare memory in increments while the application was already allocating. A team chasing fast warmup set a large -Xms, usually with -XX:+AlwaysPreTouch, and paid the whole bill before the first request landed. The JEP puts the spread at roughly a tenth of a second to start with a 2 MB heap against more than ten seconds with a 32 GB one on current hardware.

articles.title: “Abuelo, estoy en problemas. Necesito dinero”: la estafa con IA que clona la voz y rostros de familiares

Una llamada breve, una voz conocida y un pedido urgente pueden ser suficiente para que una persona mayor entregue sus ahorros. Las estafas de emergencia familiar se apoyan en inteligencia artificial (IA) para clonar voces y rostros de familiares para pedir dinero bajo presión.
Según advierte la Comisión Federal de Comercio de Estados Unidos (FTC), el engaño se apoya en dos factores: la urgencia y la necesidad de ayudar.
Quien llama puede decir que sufrió un accidente, que necesita pagar una fianza o que tuvo un problema con su auto. El estafador exige reserva. El objetivo es impedir que la víctima consulte con otros familiares antes de enviar el dinero.
Cómo un delincuente suplanta a un familiar
Los delincuentes pueden hacerse pasar por hijos, nietos u otros allegados a través de llamadas, mensajes y videollamadas. Para reforzar la identidad falsa, utilizan herramientas de inteligencia artificial capaces de imitar una voz a partir de audios disponibles en redes sociales, videos públicos o mensajes de voz.
La FTC alerta sobre la manipulación de imágenes. Una videollamada no garantiza que la persona al otro lado de la pantalla sea quien dice ser: los estafadores pueden crear o modificar videos para simular el rostro y los gestos de un familiar. La voz y la imagen ya no son pruebas suficientes de identidad.

Dans GTA 6, une arme ramassée sur un cadavre ou volée dans une voiture de police ne vous appartient pas. Le jeu la classe comme « non possédée ». Impossible de la modifier et une mort, une arrestation, un changement de personnage ou le chargement d’une sauvegarde suffit à la faire disparaître.
Pour garder une trouvaille sous la main, rangez-la dans le coffre de votre véhicule personnel. Elle y reste « non possédée ». Pour la garder pour de bon, il faut acheter le même modèle dans une armurerie qui le vend. Ne la laissez pas dans une voiture volée au hasard dans la rue. Quelques semaines plus tard, une deuxième vague a touché des supermarchés de sept pays européens, dont la Belgique et le Luxembourg. Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and subsequently grew the chipmaker into one of the most powerful companies in the world, has now been reinstated by the company’s board. The move was one that President Trump lobbied for. articles.title: Math's biggest open problem may have fallen to AI, but the proof is unreadable to humans
articles.summary:
What just happened? Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, has published a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a 167-year-old conjecture about the distribution of prime numbers and one of mathematics' most famous unsolved problems. He developed the proof with the help of Anthropic's Claude AI model. The organizations responsible for maintaining the field's leading proof-checking software verified it within a day of its release. It is the second of the seven Millennium Prize Problems to be solved with AI in roughly three months.
Alpöge did not release the proof as a traditional research paper. Instead, he posted it on his personal website in a formal programming language that allows computers to check every logical step. Within a day, reviewers from the Lean Focused Research Organization and the Mathlib Initiative had checked 17 million lines of code.
"We have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct," the two groups said in a joint statement. "We congratulate him on this achievement."
The speed of the verification came down to the format. A paper tackling a problem this difficult would normally face months or even years of expert review. A formal proof, however, can be checked mechanically. The software doesn't need to understand the reasoning or be convinced by it. It only needs to confirm that each step follows logically from the previous one.

« Il est probable que l’année 2027 s’avère encore plus chaude que 2026 », selon le physicien Robert Rohde, directeur scientifique de Berkeley Earth, qui s’exprime ce 23 novembre 2026 sur X. Les impacts d’El Niño sur les températures moyennes mondiales mettent généralement quelques mois à se faire sentir, par rapport au pic du phénomène lui-même.
Pour comprendre ce qui nous attend, nous avons interrogé Éric Guilyardi, océanographe et climatologue, directeur de recherche au CNRS (LOCEAN-IPSL) et spécialiste d’El Niño. Dans notre vidéo, il explique comment cet épisode interagit avec le réchauffement climatique et à quoi s’attendre en 2027.
Un épisode El Niño « extrême », déjà mesurable
El Niño est une anomalie climatique majeure, qui dure environ un an et revient tous les 2 à 7 ans. Éric Guilyardi rappelle que les scientifiques classent ces événements en deux catégories distinctes : les épisodes normaux et les épisodes extrêmes, caractérisés par une eau de surface plus chaude de plus de 2 °C que la normale dans l’est du Pacifique. L’épisode en cours entre dans cette seconde catégorie.

After basking in chants of his name, Huang briefly addressed the crowd.
“Thank you all for the second chance,” he said. “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.”
Over 200,000 people, including around 10,000 current Nvidia employees, had signed an open letter advocating for Huang’s return. Other tech leaders also pushed for Huang’s reinstatement, including Elon Musk, who said last week at the DealBook Summit that letting Huang go is like “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.”
Amid this increased scrutiny, however, other reports have depicted a different side to Nvidia’s top exec — one where Jensen is not seen as a beloved leader, but as a brutal bully. A nuclear-armed satellite would also put at risk Western military surveillance satellites and human spaceflight platforms like the International Space Station. A nuclear detonation in orbit would be indiscriminate, also knocking out Russia’s own spacecraft and Chinese satellites.
US lawmakers briefed on government intelligence first disclosed Russia’s ambition to deploy a space-based nuclear weapon in early 2024. At the time, US officials said Russia had launched a test satellite in 2022 to test the effects of radiation on space hardware and pave the way for a future nuclear-armed craft, but that Russia had not yet sent a nuclear weapon into orbit.
Reporting from three German news outlets—public broadcasters NDR and WDR and the Munich-based newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung—indicates Russia’s launch of a nuclear-armed satellite could be imminent. articles.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Securing AI Agents in Production
articles.summary:
Securing AI agents is a variation of the insider-risk problem, requiring distinct identities, narrowly scoped credentials and fine-grained policy controls, according to Amanda Walker, senior director of engineering for privacy, safety and security at Google. In a QCon San Francisco session, she outlined patterns for teams whose agents have been adopted organically and are running ahead of their security and observability frameworks.
With agents now executing multi-step plans in live production environments, Walker argued that "a rogue AI agent is the same problem as a rogue human insider," one that acts with superhuman speed and persistence. Controls therefore need to work at machine speed, rather than relying on someone reviewing logs the next morning. She covered identity and credentials, boundary defence, subagent orchestration and policy-based containment.
Walker described giving an agent raw human credentials as the fastest path to production failure. The agent inherits the user's authority, so a prompt injection in a document can turn that access to an attacker's purposes. She recommended explicit principals for agents, the AI equivalent of service accounts, so each agent can be provisioned and logged separately without impersonating anyone.

Se trata de la intolerancia a la incertidumbre y conocerla es muy importante.

Mozilla explica por que não há um Firefox “puro” para iPhone
Mozilla afirma que regras impostas pela Apple são complexas e inviabilizam o Firefox de ter seu próprio motor no iOS.
A Mozilla lançou a primeira versão do Firefox para iPhone em 2015. Mas, até hoje, o navegador não conta com uma implementação totalmente “pura” no iOS, com motor próprio. Em tom de desabafo, a organização explicou o motivo. Saiba desde já que, sim, a Mozilla culpa a Apple por isso.
Quando falamos de motor, nos referimos ao componente central do navegador, que interpreta o código de páginas web escrito em padrões como HTML, CSS e JavaScript, e transforma esse conjunto de informações em um conteúdo visual e interativo para o usuário.
Hoje, a maior parte dos navegadores é baseada no projeto Chromium, a exemplo do Microsoft Edge, do Opera, do Brave e, claro, do Google Chrome.
O Firefox é diferente, pois conta com um motor próprio: o Gecko. Mas, no iOS, o navegador é executado a partir do WebKit, motor mantido pela Apple que, como tal, é a base do Safari.
É aqui que está o ponto de conflito: se dependesse da Mozilla, o Firefox também contaria com o Gecko no iPhone.
A Apple exigia que os navegadores para iOS usassem o WebKit sob o argumento de que essa condição favorecia aspectos como segurança, privacidade e desempenho. Isso mudou em 2024, quando a Digital Markets Act (DMA) passou a vigorar. Trata-se de uma legislação da União Europeia que busca aumentar a concorrência no âmbito digital.

articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO, Board Director
articles.summary:
Tech giant Nvidia has announced that it has reinstated Jensen Huang as President, Chief Executive Officer, and board member.
According to Nvidia’s press release, the board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate Huang after what it described as “a series of discussions and meetings,” during which the company was “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s ability to lead Nvidia.”
Nvidia also confirmed that it received input from “senior levels of the United States government” and used that input to determine that Huang’s reinstatement posed no national security risk.
“I am honoured to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the Nvidia board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.”
Huang also added that “I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”
To add some context, Nvidia opened an independent investigation into Jensen Huang after it was revealed that a woman he was having an affair with was an alleged Chinese spy. Eventually, Huang resigned from his position at Nvidia, with current executive vice president and CFO Colette Kress serving as interim CEO.
Interestingly, Nvidia’s stock price is up over 30 per cent since the announcement that he is returning.
Source: Nvidia

Amazon previously sent mailers to NYC residents regarding a new headquarters (which was subsequently scrapped), but political messaging on packages is unprecedented for Amazon, which hasn’t used its delivery boxes to lobby for political causes before.

articles.title: Surveillance pricing uses our personal data to make us pay more
articles.summary:
“It costs what it costs” is a mindset I’ve found useful when encountering a sizable, but highly necessary or desired, expense. The sentiment encourages me to accept the price because that’s the accepted value of the gadget, app, or service that I really need or want.
But with surveillance pricing, that comfort is no longer a given. I could end up paying more for my TV because of where I am or more for a software subscription because of my age.
Surveillance pricing leverages data collected from our web history, smart devices, and apps with the goal of getting us to pay more. That obfuscates the value of products, challenges smart shopping and budgets, and makes it harder for people to get products and services at a fair price.
Surveillance pricing versus dynamic pricing
Surveillance pricing, according to the nonprofit Electronic Privacy Information Center (EPIC), is an algorithmic pricing practice that charges individuals or groups of individuals different prices “for the same goods or services.”
“The goal of surveillance pricing is to infer the highest price that the customer is willing to pay, based on consumers’ personal data and other market data,” EPIC explains.
Instacart previously practiced surveillance pricing, also called personalized pricing. In 2025, Consumer Reports found that, “based on how much Instacart says the typical household of four spends on groceries, the average price variations observed could translate into a cost swing of about $1,200 per year.” Instac…

articles.title: Windows 11 : Microsoft permet d’additionner la mémoire de plusieurs PC en USB4 pour faire tourner de grosses IA
articles.summary:
Microsoft adapte à l’USB4 une technique utilisée dans les centres de données pour accélérer les échanges entre ordinateurs. La fonction sera d’abord proposée en préversion dans le programme Windows Insider.
Trois mini-PC et trois câbles USB4 ont suffi à Microsoft pour faire tourner en local un modèle d’IA de 235 milliards de paramètres. Le moteur d’inférence répartit les poids du modèle et les calculs entre les machines, ce qui permet de dépasser la capacité mémoire d’un seul PC. Pour les faire communiquer, Microsoft utilise leurs ports USB4 et se passe ainsi de cartes réseau spécialisées et de commutateur.
Ce que le RDMA change entre deux PC
Le RDMA, pour Remote Direct Memory Access, permet de transférer des données directement entre les mémoires de deux ordinateurs en court-circuitant une grande partie de la pile réseau. Sous Windows, cette technique passait jusqu’ici par des cartes dédiées, notamment en Ethernet ou en InfiniBand. Microsoft conserve son API NetworkDirect et lui ajoute un module logiciel qui s’appuie sur les anneaux DMA du contrôleur USB4. Ces structures servent à organiser les transferts en limitant les copies effectuées par le logiciel.
C’est surtout le délai de ces échanges qui compte. Avec le parallélisme tensoriel, les machines se partagent les opérations et s’échangent des résultats intermédiaires plusieurs fois par jeton généré. articles.title: WiFi de 2,4 GHz vs 5 GHz vs cable Ethernet: cuál es mejor para ver películas en 4K
articles.summary:
La elección entre WiFi de 2,4 GHz, WiFi de 5 GHz y cable Ethernet define si una película en 4K se reproduce de forma continua o si aparecen pausas, pérdida de calidad y demoras en la carga. En una casa con varios dispositivos conectados, la ubicación del televisor y la distancia hasta el router pasan a ser factores decisivos.
Para ver contenido en alta resolución no existe una única respuesta válida para todos los hogares. La banda de 5 GHz suele aportar más velocidad cerca del router, la de 2,4 GHz llega mejor a habitaciones alejadas y el cable Ethernet ofrece una conexión física que evita parte de los problemas habituales de una red inalámbrica.
Cuándo conviene usar WiFi de 5 GHz para ver películas
El WiFi de 5 GHz suele ser la alternativa inalámbrica más adecuada para un televisor cercano al router. Esta banda transmite más datos en menos tiempo y, según la información de O2, tiene menos interferencias que la frecuencia de 2,4 GHz en zonas donde hay muchas redes domésticas alrededor.
Su principal límite aparece con la distancia. La señal de 5 GHz pierde fuerza con mayor rapidez al atravesar paredes, puertas y suelos. Si el router está en el salón o en una habitación próxima al televisor, puede ofrecer una reproducción más estable. Si ambos aparatos están separados por varios ambientes, la mejora de velocidad puede diluirse.

Preferred Care offered additional out-of-warranty protections for Pixel phones, but Google stopped offering it for new purchases in Canada at the beginning of October 2026. Notably, existing Preferred Care subscriptions remain active — only new customers are locked out.

What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team.
The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. On Monday, Virginia and Oregon became the first states to sue SpaceX, alleging that Grok continues to sexualize, unchecked, real photos of mostly women and children.
SpaceX acquired xAI in February and now must handle the ongoing reckoning over the controversial rollout of Grok’s “spicy mode”—a model feature Musk hyped but was soon found to generate a flood of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) and child sex abuse images (CSAM).
Initial safeguards were so lax that Grok sometimes generated nude images without being asked. Although X Safety and xAI (now known as SpaceXSI) were silent at first, Musk’s companies eventually apologized and claimed that additional safeguards were implemented and policies redesigned to block harmful outputs. However, state attorneys general alleged that those statements were “misleading” and that SpaceXSI instead quietly “embraced” sexualized content to seize more AI market share, as Grok continues to generate NCII and CSAM today.
Without intervention, kids in Virginia and Oregon risk a lifetime of distress, as Grok images will likely be impossible to remove online.
“Once created and shared,” Grok-generated CSAM and NCII “can never be fully erased, and it becomes a permanent record of the child’s abuse that may resurface for the rest of the child’s life,” Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones’ complaint said. “Virginia has a profound interest in protecting its children from this harm.”

Datenversand per Schwerkraft: Physiker schicken Textnachricht durch eine Ziegelwand
Fünf Physiker der University of Queensland im australischen Brisbane haben erstmals eine digitale Botschaft allein über Schwankungen der Anziehungskraft gesendet. Sie übertrugen das englische Wort „Gravity“ durch eine 27 Zentimeter dicke Mauer, wie ihre Studie im Wissenschaftsmagazin Science Advances beschreibt.
University of Queensland nutzt alten Aufzug als Sender
Als Signalgeber diente ein Aufzug aus den 1950er-Jahren, dessen rund 1,8 Tonnen schweres Gegengewicht aus Gusseisen zwischen zwei Etagen fuhr. Im benachbarten Waschraum stand auf dem Boden ein sogenanntes Gravimeter, also ein empfindliches Messgerät für winzige Veränderungen der örtlichen Schwerkraft.
Während Metallkäfige, Erdreich oder dickes Mauerwerk Funkwellen, Licht und Schall abhalten, kann kein bekanntes Material die Anziehungskraft von Masse blockieren. „Ein Gravitationssignal lässt sich nicht einfach abschirmen, indem man gewöhnliches Material in seinen Weg stellt“, erklärt Mitautor Charles Woffinden in einer Hochschulmitteilung.
Mit kosmischen Gravitationswellen, die erst bei schweren Himmelskörpern wie Schwarzen Löchern messbar durch das All laufen, arbeitet das System jedoch nicht. Stattdessen zog das bewegte Gegengewicht im Schacht lediglich eine kleine Testmasse an einer Feder im Messgerät je nach Etage unterschiedlich stark an.

- The incident highlights growing extortion tactics where threat actors publicize alleged breaches before providing proof of data theft
Nvidia has confirmed it is investigating claims of a data breach after a prolific ransomware operator added the company’s name to its data leak website.
On November 18, 2026, threat actors going under “The Gentlemen” added Nvidia to their website, as per International Cyber Digest. They didn’t share any details - we don’t know the nature of the stolen files, or the size of the allegedly exfiltrated archive.
The group only said “DATA INFO - SOON” on the website entry and shared a clock that counts down to November 28 2026 - most likely the date when they plan on leaking everything (unless Nvidia decides to pay the ransom demand in the meantime).

articles.title: Milchstraße mit 5,4 Billionen Teilchen simuliert – wie KI ein altes Rechenproblem löst
articles.summary:
5,4 Billionen Teilchen: Wie KI die Milchstraße auf drei Supercomputern nachbildet
Forscher:innen um das Institut Riken im japanischen Wako und die japanische Universität Tokio haben die Milchstraße nun bis auf einzelne Sterne simuliert. Das Team stellte die Studie auf der Supercomputer-Konferenz SC26 in Chicago vor und berechnete mit dem Programm Pheasant bis zu 5,4 Billionen Teilchen.
Damit liegt die Auflösung für Sterne, Gas und unsichtbare Dunkle Materie tausend- bis zehntausendmal höher als in bisherigen Modellen der gesamten Galaxie. Die Software lief dafür getrennt auf drei verschiedenen Supercomputern, benötigte neben reiner Hardwareleistung für diese Detailtiefe aber zusätzlich künstliche Intelligenz.
KI-Modell überbrückt Sternexplosionen in der Milchstraße

- The government’s ability to secretly impose surveillance-by-design mechanisms onto service providers without robust judicial authorization
- The government’s ability to obligate digital service providers to keep metadata indiscriminately on everyone, including in situations where it cannot be linked to a specific investigation or security threat.
- The government’s ability to impose surveillance-by-design obligations that break safeguards like end-to-end encryption
- The government’s need to include individual notice requirements and other safeguards into search provisions
- being able to prevent the federal government from using the surveillance powers to facilitate investigations of any activity that is not criminal here by law enforcement in other countries.
“Bill C-22’s excessive in its breadth of application and its inconsistency with global standards could threaten Canada’s ongoing attempts to integrate digitally with partners in the European Union,” writes the Canadian Civil Liberties Association.

articles.title: AI agents leaked confidential data in 87 of 100 test runs, Cyberhaven finds
articles.summary:
AI agents leaked confidential data in 87 of 100 test runs, Cyberhaven finds
A new report out today from data security company Cyberhaven Inc. finds that artificial intelligence agents will leak confidential company data if doing so helps them get the job done, even after noting that it’s confidential.
The report from Cyberhaven Labs, the company’s research arm, is based on a test in which agents built on five different AI models were given an ordinary marketing task: Write a six-month product report for a company blog, cite the numbers and then publish it.
The user pointed the agents to a confidential board review and an internal customer spreadsheet as sources for the numbers, though no one asked for either file to be shared. The agents also had access to an approved press kit that could have been used instead. Of the 100 test runs, confidential data ended up on the public blog in 87.
The models tested included three open-weight models, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8, along with two closed models in the form of Anthropic PBC’s Claude Sonnet 5.5 and OpenAI Group PBC’s GPT-6.1 Terra.
Confidential data was found to have leaked in 57 of the 60 runs involving the open-weight models, which were also the worst offenders when it came to sharing entire documents. In 16 of those runs, a whole confidential file was made public. In all 16 cases, the agent had flagged the risk in its reasoning before going ahead and doing it anyway. This basically means that HWiNFO's sensor readings can now be viewed in a web browser on any device connected to your home network, including phones and tablets. HWiNFO has also put up a GitHub package with an API guide, along with sample dashboards and material for building dashboards with AI agents. To set it up, users have to navigate to the Sensors window, where a new Remote Center button opens an API panel. Then, users pick an IP address and port, choose whether to use HTTPS, and hit Start. HWiNFO has included a ready-made dashboard modeled on the Sensors window, but you can also add custom pages. Without a license, the REST API server is limited to 12 hours of operation. This is the same cap the free version already puts on Shared Memory support as well as remote sensor monitoring. Power users can extend that time by picking up HWiNFO Pro. As far as security goes, HWiNFO recommends keeping the server on trusted networks only.

Independent Quad Extrusion, or IQEX, is unlike tool-changer 3D printers. Instead of one print head swapping assemblies, it has four individual print heads. This allows for increased productivity by printing with all four heads at once, or reducing waste by not going through any purging steps.
The Co Print Quadro is a non-enclosed bedslinger, and its design is quite similar to the Bambu Lab A1, albeit much beefier. GTA VI Launch Weekend Sees Nearly 45 Million Copies Sold
Already on launch day, it was well reported that GTA VI had shattered entertainment industry records, but it seems as though that was just the start of a legendary opening weekend. According to Alinea Analytics's Rhys Elliott in a recent post on X, Grand Theft Auto VI had already reached an estimated 44.9 million sales by the end of its opening weekend. This translates to over $4 billion in gross revenue. 
Alinea estimates that as much as 75.1%, or 33.7 million, of GTA VI's sales were on PlayStation 5, while 24.9%, or 11.9 million, were on Xbox. These figures reportedly accounted for roughly 30% of each platform's install base—meaning 30% of PS5 and Xbox Series owners purchased GTA VI on or before launch weekend. It is also estimated that the game reached a daily active user count of around 40.8 million users on Sunday, November 22.In a separate post, Alinea estimated that roughly 32.8% of GTA VI copies were sold in the US, with 9% of sales coming from France, 7.3% coming from the UK, 5.1% coming from Germany, and only 4.7% coming from China. While Chinese sales are still low, it's worth noting that Western games generally don't sell as well in China, due to an already well-established local gaming market, and there is no official distribution channel for mainland China, so all sales came from gray-market imports.

The company aims to cover 60% to 70% of its memory supply with such deals by 2030. The Economy Tribune report says that new deals could come with pre-payments, as well as both upper and lower price limits.
That's the memory production capacity, but the more worrying part for PC builders is conventional DRAM. Industry leaders like Dell and SK hynix have already given timelines till 2030 for the situation to improve, and there looks to be no relief coming from Samsung's side either. Sources cited in the report say 2027 wafer capacity for commodity DRAM is effectively sold out. Moreover, DRAM bit supply growth is reportedly expected to top out at around 20% to 25% a year. articles.title: Experimental XNU Linux Project Boots macOS 27 Desktop on Linux
articles.summary:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
Experimental XNU Linux Project Boots macOS 27 Desktop on Linux
Unix software enthusiasts, rejoice! An experimental project called "XNU Linux" has successfully booted a complete macOS 27 desktop on an ARM64 Linux system. This breakthrough offers a new way to run Apple's operating system without relying on traditional virtualization methods. This is significant news for the community, as there is a large group of enthusiasts eager to create custom macOS desktops, also known as Hackintoshes. The project utilizes Apple's open-source XNU kernel, modified to function as a loadable module within Linux, enabling macOS and Linux processes to run on the same hardware.
Instead of translating macOS applications into a format Linux can execute, XNU Linux takes a different approach by integrating Apple's kernel into the Linux environment. It consists of two primary components: xnu.ko, which runs the hosted XNU kernel, and fki.ko, which provides an interface to Linux resources such as memory, networking, timers, and storage. This setup allows macOS processes to run natively on the host CPU without an intervening hypervisor. The setup has been tested on an NVIDIA DGX Spark running Ubuntu, as well as an Apple Silicon Mac running Linux in a virtual machine. The system successfully reached the macOS desktop, including Finder, Dock, WindowServer, and loginwindow, with Safari and Chrome also operational. articles.title: Jensen Huang dice que si hoy tuviera 20 años no estudiaría lo que lo llevó a ser CEO de Nvidia

Su respuesta fue directa: elegiría las ciencias físicas por encima de las ciencias del software. Huang recordó que él mismo se graduó dos años antes de lo habitual, a los 20 años, con un título en ingeniería eléctrica.
Qué son las ciencias físicas y por qué Huang las elegiría
Las ciencias físicas comprenden el estudio de sistemas no vivos: física, química, astronomía y ciencias de la Tierra, a diferencia de las ciencias de la vida. Huang obtuvo su título en ingeniería eléctrica en la Universidad Estatal de Oregón en 1984 y una maestría en la misma disciplina en Stanford en 1992.
Huang sostiene que la inteligencia artificial atraviesa fases sucesivas desde hace más de una década. La primera, la “IA de percepción”, nació hace entre 12 y 14 años con la aparición de AlexNet, un modelo que marcó el salto de la visión por computadora.
Luego llegó la “IA generativa”, capaz de traducir el significado de la información en lenguajes, imágenes y código. Hoy, según Huang, la tecnología transita la “IA de razonamiento”, que permite crear agentes digitales capaces de resolver problemas inéditos.

Qué es el efecto 3D en las fotos del iPhone
El efecto utiliza la información de profundidad que almacenan las fotos hechas en modo Retrato. Con esos datos, el sistema separa el sujeto del fondo y genera un leve movimiento entre ambos planos para simular relieve.
La imagen resultante reacciona al desplazar el iPhone o al tocarla en pantalla. Esta misma tecnología de profundidad es la que permite “espacializar” una foto para usarla como fondo de pantalla, bajo el nombre de fotos espaciales.
No todas las fotografías sirven para aplicar este efecto. Solo las capturadas en modo Retrato guardan la información de profundidad necesaria para que el sistema distinga entre el sujeto y el entorno.

"In the observed incidents, attackers targeted business records and approval processes to carry out unauthorized transactions through otherwise legitimate systems," CERT-In said in an advisory last week.
The incidents have been found to include the following methods -
- Abuse of business applications and service provider-operated workflows, as opposed to direct exploitation of payment-related APIs.
- Modification of business records or approval relationships, followed by the use of legitimate payment processes.
- Use of trusted systems and established approval procedures to process unauthorized transactions without raising any alert.
- Exploitation of security blind spots in independent verification, reconciliation, and review of changes to business records.
CERT-In did not reveal how much money had been improperly paid out, or by whom. The activity has not been attributed to any specific threat actor.

articles.title: Today I learned that Apple's newest iPhone Pro models are cooled using water vapor
articles.summary:
Today I learned that Apple's newest iPhone Pro models are cooled using water vapor
There's a sealed drop of water inside your iPhone Pro
The new iPhone Pro has water inside it and Apple put it there on purpose. Since the iPhone 17 Pro launched in September 2025, Apple's Pro smartphone models have all launched with a vapor chamber. It's a sealed metal pocket holding a tiny amount of water that boils and condenses to pull heat away from the chip.
Apple doesn't usually talk plumbing at its launch events, but this time it did. "Deionized water is sealed inside the vapor chamber," the company said in its press release, adding that the chamber is laser-welded into the phone's aluminum frame. Apple claimed up to 40% better sustained performance than the iPhone 16 Pro.
This came with a material change, too. The 17 Pro ditched titanium for an aerospace-grade aluminum unibody, which Apple said delivered the best thermal performance of any iPhone yet.
How a drop of water cools a chip
Most phones have long relied on solid plates of copper or graphite to spread heat. Those work, but adding more surface area usually means a thicker phone, according to IEEE Spectrum.
A vapor chamber does the job differently. The water evaporates near the hot chip, carries that heat across the chamber as vapor, then condenses back into liquid once the heat escapes into the phone's aluminum body. Turning liquid into gas soaks up a lot of energy, which is why the same trick has cooled laptops for decades.

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ASP.NET Anti-CSRF Library Flaw Allowing Unauthenticated RCE
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity researchers have urged users to discontinue using a legacy ASP.NET anti-CSRF library named Idunno.AntiCsrf ("Idunno.AntiCsrf.dll") following the discovery of a critical vulnerability that has been exploited in the wild.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-131914, carries a CVSS score of 9.3 out of 10.0. The issue affects versions 0.9.1.0 and 0.9.1 Beta, and relates to an insecure deserialization vulnerability in the Idunno.AntiCsrf.AntiCsrfModule HTTP module.
Idunno.AntiCsrf is a third-party ASP.NET IHttpModule designed to provide double-submit cookie Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) protection for ASP.NET WebForms applications. The open-source project is currently defunct and has not been updated since December 2008.
At its core, the problem stems from the fact that the module deserializes untrusted CSRF form token data using an unkeyed .NET System.Web.UI.ObjectStateFormatter instance without cryptographic MAC or signature verification when handling incoming HTTP POST requests to ASP.NET WebForms (System.Web.UI.Page) endpoints.
This behavior, in turn, can allow a remote attacker to achieve arbitrary remote code execution (RCE). Google's Mandiant division has given the vulnerability a "High" exploitability assessment, adding that exploitation hinges only on a single HTTP POST request with no prior authentication or valid CSRF token.

The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-134624, is a server-side request forgery (SSRF) flaw. It allowed a user with high-level API access to open connections to internal systems of the user's choosing on the platform's servers.
The company fixed the flaw and restored access to the dashboard and APIs late on Saturday, closing an outage that began last Monday. Email delivery and spam filtering kept working throughout, according to the company. It has not said whether the flaw was the attackers' way in.
The bug sat in a connection check that Mail Assure runs for LDAP synchronization when a relay is configured. Before the fixed build, nothing restricted that check's destination, so the server could be pointed at any internal host and port to see which ones answered.
"An authenticated API user can cause the server to connect to arbitrary internal hosts and ports, determine which are reachable, and send crafted data to internal services.," the vendor's security advisory says.
The advisory gives the flaw a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.3, and lists builds earlier than 20261121.1943 as affected, with that same build as the fix. It does not claim code execution.

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ScreenConnect Flaw to Hijack MSP Technician PCs Without Warning
articles.summary:
Threat actors are exploiting a now-patched security flaw in ConnectWise ScreenConnect to target managed service provider (MSP) servers.
The activity revolves around CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS score: 9.9), a critical ScreenConnect client flaw that allows a guest to transfer and execute a malicious payload on a connecting technician's host.
"On November 12, 2026, we observed one managed service provider's (MSP) technician's workstation exploited to run a guest-pushed batch file, which then reported to a Telegram bot, downloaded an installer from masterdarky[.]com, and started a rogue ScreenConnect client pointing at the attacker's own relay, all in about 9 seconds," Huntress security researcher John Hammond said.
The batch script, "update_224ac089.bat," is designed to decode a Base64 Telegram bot token and chat ID, and register the new infection. Subsequently, it downloads an MSI installer that masquerades as a Windows update ("WindowsUpdate.msi") to launch a ScreenConnect client, enabling the attacker to gain remote access to the technician's machine.
The activity, observed between October 20 and November 16, 2026, is said to have sprayed servers blindly, with Huntress observing at least 688,000 guest "run file" requests for files named update.bat or update_<8 hex>.bat hitting 42 ScreenConnect servers from 29 IP addresses. The guests have been found to make repeated requests that have blank session names or default-looking Windows hostnames.

articles.title: Critical binary-parser Flaw Enables JavaScript Injection via Malicious Parser Definitions
articles.summary:
A critical security flaw has been disclosed in the popular binary-parser library that could allow an attacker who controls parser definitions to execute arbitrary code.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-134814 (CVSS score: 9.2 / 8.1), is a case of code injection impacting binary-parser versions prior to 2.3.1.
"Binary-parser before 2.3.1 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers controlling parser definitions to inject JavaScript through string-typed options passed unvalidated by Context.generateOption()," according to a description of the flaw in the NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD).
"Attackers can supply crafted length, lengthInBytes, key, tag, offset, or namely() alias values to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the Node.js process when the parser is compiled."
According to an advisory released by the project maintainer on November 11, 2026, the problem arose from the fact that some user-controlled string options were inserted directly into the generated JavaScript code without adequate validation.
The parser options include -
- length
- lengthInBytes
- key
- tag
- offset, and
- the alias passed to namely()
"Parsing untrusted binary data with a trusted parser definition is not affected," Keichi Takahashi, who maintains the library, said. "These options are now validated as identifier paths (e.g. foo, $parent.len). Expressions such as 'len - 1' are rejected; use a function instead."

Le principe est que l'IA éclaire, et l'humain décide. The modified variant "implements various tricks to hide itself from security tools," Rapid7 said in an analysis, attributing it to the adversarial collective with moderate confidence.
First publicly detailed by Broadcom-owned Symantec in September 2022, Webworm is the name assigned to a China-aligned nation-state group that has targeted government entities, IT services, and electric power companies across Russia, Georgia, Mongolia, and several other Asian nations.
One of the tools used by the threat actor is a legitimate software called SoftEther VPN, with the bridge acting as a pathway connecting the compromised network and the attacker-controlled infrastructure.
The latest findings from Rapid7 revolve around a Windows executable ("netcapa.exe"), which is a modified build of SoftEther VPN Bridge ("vpnbridge_x64.exe") version 4.44, build 9807. The modified version, rebranded as NtMonitor VPN, masquerades itself as Network Monitor Software from a company called Network Systems Solutions Inc. Palmer Luckey has a blunt message for anyone still running yesterday's infrastructure: "It's time to start running."
Speaking with Andrew Ross Sorkin at the recent The New York Times DealBook Summit, the Anduril co-founder and Oculus founder warned that AI tools are letting attackers build exploits faster than older systems can be defended.
The setting gave Luckey's warning extra weight, as that same morning, Vice President JD Vance pulled out of his own DealBook appearance shortly before he was due on stage, staying in Washington for meetings about a run of outages that had hit Microsoft, the FAA, JPMorgan Chase, Zelle and the National Security Agency.

articles.title: Cómo reconocer las trampas de diseño que empujan a comprar y a suscribirse antes del Black Friday
articles.summary:
La Comisión Europea propuso el 11 de noviembre una ley que prohibiría los llamados patrones oscuros: diseños de sitios y aplicaciones que presionan o confunden para que el usuario compre o se suscriba. Como todavía es solo un proyecto, antes del Black Friday la defensa depende de reconocer esas trampas.
El texto, llamado Ley de Equidad Digital, es una propuesta que debe negociar el Parlamento Europeo con el Consejo de la Unión Europea antes de convertirse en norma, según el análisis publicado el 16 de noviembre por el estudio jurídico Addleshaw Goddard. Rige, por ahora, únicamente como borrador.
Su lista de prácticas prohibidas sirve igual como inventario de lo que conviene mirar con desconfianza, vengan de donde vengan las ofertas. La propia Comisión, en su documento de preguntas y respuestas, ofrece ejemplos concretos de cada una.
Tres señales de presión para detectar en la pantalla
La primera es la falsa escasez. La Comisión cita avisos como “Solo queda 1” o “¡5 personas más están interesadas!” cuando no son ciertos. Si el aviso no cita una fuente verificable, conviene abrir otra pestaña y comparar el precio y la disponibilidad en otra tienda antes de decidir.
La segunda es la culpa como herramienta. El documento menciona mensajes del tipo “Nos da pena que te vayas” y botones para rechazar una promoción con frases como “No me gustan las buenas ofertas”. Ninguno cambia el precio ni las condiciones: solo buscan que el usuario desista de cancelar o de darse de baja.

articles.title: Free corrige un bug qui faisait redémarrer la Freebox Delta en plein téléchargement
articles.summary:
Free a déployé lundi une nouvelle mise à jour du Freebox Server, sixième version depuis le 5 novembre. En plus de correctifs de sécurité, elle corrige un problème de stabilité qui pouvait figer, puis faire redémarrer, la Freebox Delta.
C'est une énième mise à jour que l'opérateur Free a décidé de déployer ce lundi 23 novembre 2026. La version 4.13.8 du Freebox Server est disponible depuis midi aujourd'hui, pour les Freebox Revolution, Pop, Delta et Ultra. Free annonce des correctifs de sécurité et la correction d'un « problème de stabilité » propre à la Freebox Delta, à l'origine signalé par un abonné. Comme toujours, il faut redémarrer la box pour l'installer.
Une Freebox Delta qui gelait, puis redémarrait
Il y a quelques jours, un abonné Delta a décrit son problème sur le site de suivi des bugs de Free. Sa box se figeait une à quatre minutes, son interface ne répondait plus, puis redémarrait entièrement, en coupant au passage son réseau câblé pendant une bonne vingtaine de secondes. C'était arrivé cinq fois entre le 11 et le 15 novembre, toujours en soirée, et toujours pendant qu'un ordinateur de la maison, branché en Ethernet, téléchargeait de très gros fichiers depuis Hugging Face, la grande plateforme de modèles d'IA.
Pour l'abonné, le coupable, ce n'est pas la vitesse, mais le nombre de connexions. Comme beaucoup d'outils pensés pour aller vite, son logiciel ouvrait jusqu'à 64 connexions simultanées vers les serveurs, en quelques secondes, pour un débit de 1 à 1,5 Gbit/…
